式内社の位置}}]] [[File:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|{{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}} 配置図}}]] In the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}}, the Kami Name Register begins by listing 36 shrines in the palace and 3 in the capital. As the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}} was compiled in the mid-{{ill|Heian Period|de|Heian-Zeit|ja|平安時代|zh|平安时代}}, “in the palace” and “in the capital” refer respectively to those within the Heian Palace ({{ill|Heian Capital|de|Heian-Hauptstadt|ja|平安京|zh|Heian Capital}}/{{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|大内裏|zh|Imperial Palace}}) and to those within the city of Heian-kyo. The following explains each enshrined deity. ; Palace Deities (30 major shrines, 6 minor shrines) : This term refers to the deities enshrined within the Imperial Palace of {{ill|Heian Capital|de|Heian-Hauptstadt|ja|平安京|zh|Heian Capital}}, as reported by {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=8}}. The rituals for the 8 Imperial Miko deities were handed down at one of the {{ill|Three Palace Sanctuaries|de|Drei Palastheiligtümer|ja|宮中三殿|zh|三宫殿}} (Shinden), and it is presumed that the worship of the other palace deities was likewise inherited within the “Tenjin-Chigi” section of the Shinden. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}} :; Deities Enshrined in the Western Wing of the {{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}} (21 shrines) ::: These are the deities enshrined at the {{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}}, one of the {{ill|Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|de|Zwei Ämter und Acht Ministerien|ja|二官八省|zh|二官八省}}. The Jingi-kan comprised an Eastern and a Western Wing (Saien); while the Eastern Wing performed administrative duties, the Western Wing handled ritual functions. The deities in the Western Wing, sometimes termed the “Emperor’s Shinto Altar” {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176}}, occupy a key position, although the ancestral deity {{ill|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|zh|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|lt=amaterasu}} is not enshrined there. These gods were served by shrine maidens known as {{ill|Miko|de|Miko|ja|巫女|zh|巫女}}, called “Mikanna.” For each served deity there were 2 chief Mikos (later 3), 1 Zasama Miko, 1 Mikado Miko, and 1 Ikushima Miko. All 21 enshrined deities were designated formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}. ::: Although the Jingi-kan declined and fell into ruin during the medieval period, its continuation is attested until the [[Ōnin]] period (from {{ill|1467th year|de|1467th year|ja|1467年|zh|1467年}} to {{ill|1468th year|de|1468th year|ja|1468年|zh|1468年}}), but by the {{ill|Bunmei Period|de|Bunmei-Ära|ja|文明|zh|文明}} (from {{ill|1469th year|de|1469th year|ja|1469年|zh|1469年}} to {{ill|1486th year|de|1486th year|ja|1486年|zh|1486年}}) it appears to have been completely abolished. In the {{ill|Tenshō Period|de|Tenshō-Ära|ja|天正|zh|天正}} 18th year ({{ill|1590th year|de|1590th year|ja|1590年|zh|1590年}}), eight Shinden were enshrined within the precincts of {{ill|Yoshida Shrine|de|Yoshida Shrine|ja|吉田神社|zh|吉田神社}}, and in the {{ill|Keichō Period|de|Keichō-Ära|ja|慶長|zh|慶长}} 14th year ({{ill|1609th year|de|1609th year|ja|1609年|zh|1609年}}) Yoshida Shrine was designated as the substitute for the Jingi-kan. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|de|Meiji-Restauration|ja|明治維新|zh|明治维新}}, a Shinden enshrining the Eight Gods and Tenjin-Chigi was built within the Imperial Palace, and the ritual practice was maintained; however, since ancient rites had become entirely extinct, the current ceremonies are completely different. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176-201}} :::; {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|lt=Mikamisai-shin|lt_ja=御巫祭神|lt_de=Mikamisai-shin|lt_zh=Mikamisai-shin}} (8 shrines: {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神}}, {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神}}, {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神}}, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}}, {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}, and {{ill|Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神}}). ::::: These 8 deities were served by the chief Miko ({{ill|Oomikanna|de|Oomikanna|ja|大御巫|zh|大御巫}}). According to the personnel regulations set out in the {{ill|Reishūkai|de|Reishūkai|ja|令集解|zh|令集解}}, in the Nara period the chief Miko system consisted of 2 “Wakoku Miko,” but by the Heian period, as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}}, it had expanded to 3—for the Emperor, the {{ill|Empress|de|Kaiserin|ja|中宮|zh|中宫}}, and the {{ill|Crown Prince|de|Kronprinz|ja|東宮|zh|东宫}}. These 8 deities, which include 5 governing souls, one mediating between ruler and subjects ({{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}}), one governing food ({{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}), and one governing language ({{ill|Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神}}), thus serve to pacify the spirit, were enshrined in the {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden}}. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} ({{ill|859th year|de|859th year|ja|859年|zh|859年}}), {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神}}, and {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神}} were promoted to First Rank, while {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神}} was raised to Second Rank. Among these, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}} is said to have passed down a small shrine in the Shuze area of Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Yoshida Shrine|de|Yoshida Shrine|ja|吉田神社|zh|吉田神社}}, is also well known. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=184-187}} :::; {{ill|Zasama-no-kami|de|Zasama-no-kami|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|lt=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_ja=座摩巫祭神|lt_de=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_zh=Zasama-mikanna-shin}} (5 shrines: {{ill|Ikuni-no-kami|de|Ikuni-no-kami|ja|生井神|zh|生井神}}, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社}}, {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神}}, {{ill|Hapihi-no-kami|de|Hapihi-no-kami|ja|波比祇神|zh|波比祇神}}, and {{ill|Asuha-no-kami|de|Asuha-no-kami|ja|阿須波神|zh|阿须波神}}). ::::: These 5 deities were served by a Zasama Miko, who—unlike the other Mikos—was stipulated in the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}} to be the daughter of the {{ill|Tokagenokuzō|de|Tokagenokuzō|ja|闘鶏国造|zh|闘鶏国造|lt=Tokagenokuzō|lt_ja=都下国造|lt_de=Tokagenokuzō|lt_zh=Tokagenokuzō}}. They comprise three deities safeguarding water and two safeguarding the premises, collectively regarded as deities protecting the palace. Their divine Ranks were elevated to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). Among these, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社}} and {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神}} are said to have transmitted a small shrine in Fukunaga-cho, Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社}}, is known in Osaka. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Zasama-shin|de|Zasama-shin|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=187-188}} :::; {{ill|Mikado-no-kami|de|Mikado-no-kami|ja|御門巫祭神|zh|御門巫祭神|lt=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_ja=櫛石窓神|lt_de=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_zh=櫛石窓神}} (8 shrines: 4 for the {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神}} and 4 for the {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神}}) ::::: These 8 deities were served by the Mikado Miko. They enshrined the four gates of the outer perimeter of the {{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|内裏|zh|内裏}}—namely, the East Gate ({{ill|Kenchunmon|de|Kenchunmon|ja|建春門|zh|建春门}}), South Gate ({{ill|Kenreimon|de|Kenreimon|ja|建礼門|zh|建礼门}}), West Gate ({{ill|Gikyuimon|de|Gikyuimon|ja|宜秋門|zh|宜秋门}}), and North Gate ({{ill|Sakuhimon|de|Sakuhimon|ja|朔平門|zh|朔平门}}). One shrine each for {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神}} and {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神}} was enshrined, although the usual festival was held at the Western Wing of the Jingi-kan. There is a theory that because the deities named “Kushiishi Mado-no-kami” and “Toyoshi Mado-no-kami” were enshrined as natural stones—similar to the four guardian deities enshrined as natural stones in the precincts of {{ill|Ise Shrine|de|Ise-Schrein|ja|伊勢神宮|zh|伊势神宫}}—they were in fact enshrined as natural stones at each gate. Their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). An associated shrine, {{ill|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|de|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|ja|櫛石窓神社|zh|櫛石窓神社}}, located in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|de|Hyōgo Prefecture|ja|兵庫県|zh|兵库县}} in {{ill|Tamba Sasayama|de|Tamba Sasayama|ja|丹波篠山市|zh|丹波篠山市}}, is regarded as the original. :::; {{ill|Ikushima-no-kami|de|Ikushima-no-kami|ja|生島神|zh|生島神}} and {{ill|Ashishima-no-kami|de|Ashishima-no-kami|ja|足島神|zh|足島神}} (2 shrines) ::::: These 2 deities were served by the Ikushima Miko. According to the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|de|Kogo Shūi|ja|古語拾遺|zh|古语拾遗}}, they are regarded as the spirits of the nation (the “Great Eight Islands”) and serve as a divine underpinning for the Emperor’s rule. Their divine Ranks were raised to Lower Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). Associated shrines include {{ill|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|de|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|ja|生國魂神社|zh|生国魂神社}} (Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture) and {{ill|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine|de|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine|ja|生島足島神社|zh|生岛足岛神社}} (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture). {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=189-192}} ::: The deities enshrined in the Jingi-kan are described as radiating outward in concentric circles—from the Emperor’s body (served by the Imperial Miko), to the palace (served by the Zasama Miko), to the outer gates (served by the Mikado Miko), and finally to the land (served by the Ikushima Miko). In particular, because associated shrines such as {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社}} and {{ill|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|de|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|ja|生國魂神社|zh|生国魂神社}} remain in Naniwa, it is theorized that the rites once performed at Naniwa Palace continued into the Heian period, with the existence of the {{ill|Ya-shima Festival|de|Ya-shima Festival|ja|八十島祭|zh|八十岛祭}} during imperial enthronements emphasizing Naniwa’s importance. {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=190-192}} ; Deities of the Imperial Household Ministry (3 shrines: Son Shrine and two Kan Shrines) ::: These refer to the deities enshrined within the {{ill|Imperial Household Ministry|de|Kaiserliches Haushaltsministerium|ja|宮内省|zh|宫内省}}, whose exact identities vary – some sources state that the Son deity protects the garden pond, others that the Kan deity wards off epidemics – but in any case they have been enshrined since before the Heian period. All are formal shrines, and their offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}; their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Third Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). For further details, see the article on {{ill|Sonkan Shrine|de|Sonkan Shrine|ja|園韓神社|zh|园韩神社}}. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Court Meals (3 shrines: Mishokutsunushi Shrine, Hurai Shrine, and Koubai Shrine) ::: These deities, under the auspices of the ministry responsible for court meals (the {{ill|Daizen-shoku|de|Daizen-shoku|ja|大膳職|zh|大膳职}}), include {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}, who governs food; {{ill|Hurai Shrine|de|Hurai Shrine|ja|火雷神社|zh|火雷神社}}, who governs water; and {{ill|Koubai Shrine|de|Koubai Shrine|ja|高倍神社|zh|高倍神社}}, associated with earthenware. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859), the divine Rank of {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}} was raised to Lower Third Rank, that of Hurai Shrine to Upper Fifth Rank, and that of Koubai Shrine to Lower Fifth Rank. According to the anecdotal record {{ill|Takahashi Shibun|de|Takahashi Shibun|ja|高橋氏文|zh|高桥氏文}}, see also [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection – Awa Zashinja (Awa Province, Awa District)] and [{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 'Gunsho Ruijū Fifth Volume'] in the National Diet Library Digital Collection, additional details are provided. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Sake Production (4 shrines at O-miyaburushi Shrine; 2 shrines at Sakaden Shrine) ::: These deities, affiliated with the ministry responsible for sake brewing (the {{ill|Zōshūsai|de|Zōshūsai|ja|造酒司|zh|造酒司}}), consist of the O-miyaburushi deity associated with food and sake and two deities governing the water used in brewing. All four O-miyaburushi shrines were formal shrines, with their offerings entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}; in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859) the divine Rank of Sakaden Shrine appears to have been raised to Lower Fifth Rank, and in the 3rd year of Jōgan ({{ill|862nd year|de|862nd year|ja|862年|zh|862年}}) the deities Sakayamitodono Otoko-no-kami and Sakayamitodono Megami were elevated to Upper Fifth Rank. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=32}} ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Water (1 shrine) ::: This is the deity enshrined in the office of the {{ill|Shusui-shi|de|Shusui-shi|ja|主水司|zh|主水司}}, which oversees water and ice procurement—the deity being enshrined at {{ill|Narutai Shrine|de|Narutai Shrine|ja|鳴雷神社|zh|鳴雷神社}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=33}} ; Capital Deities (3 shrines: Taishikoto-no-mikoto, Hisashimitachinomiya, and Hayai Shrine) : These are the deities enshrined within the capital of Heian-kyo, as listed in the Kami Name Register. All three are formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}, and particularly the deities Taishikoto-no-mikoto and Hisashimitachinomiya were also honored at the {{ill|Sounamatsuri|de|Sounamatsuri|ja|相嘗祭|zh|相嘗祭}}. ; {{ill|Ame-no-Osoroshi-no-mikoto|de|Ame-no-Osoroshi-no-mikoto|ja|天児屋命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天児屋命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|lt=Taitatari-no-mikoto|lt_ja=太詔戸命神|lt_de=Taitatari-no-mikoto|lt_zh=Taitatari-no-mikoto}} :: In the Muromachi period, this deity of ritual recitations (prayers) was enshrined to the west. His divine Rank was raised to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859), later to Upper Third Rank. He is now defunct. In the Kami Name Register he appears as the formal shrine in Yamato Province—namely, the “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with Mori Shrine in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|de|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|zh|奈良县}}/{{ill|Tenri City|de|Tenri City|ja|天理市|zh|天理市}}) and in Tsushima Province as “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with {{ill|Taishikoto Shrine|de|Taishikoto Shrine|ja|太祝詞神社|zh|太祝詞神社}} in {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|de|Nagasaki Prefecture|ja|長崎県|zh|长崎县}}/{{ill|Tsushima City|de|Tsushima City|ja|対馬市|zh|对马市}}); these are regarded as his original enclosures. ; {{ill|Kushimachinomiya|de|Kushimachinomiya|ja|櫛真智命|zh|櫛真智命|lt=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_ja=久慈真智命神|lt_de=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_zh=Hisashimitachinomiya}} :: Enshrined to the west of the Shijōbōmon area, this divinized deity of divination was elevated to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859) and is now defunct. According to the Kami Name Register, his original shrine is the “Tenkōzan Zari Kushinomiya Shrine” in Yamato Province (with candidate shrines in [[Kashihara City]] of Nara Prefecture, including Tenkōzan Shrine and Kuninotokotachi Shrine) and is considered his original. ; {{ill|Hayai Shrine|de|Hayai Shrine|ja|隼神社|zh|隼神社}} :: Enshrined within the Shujakuin of the Later Palace, this deity was raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the sixteenth year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} ({{ill|874th year|de|874th year|ja|874年|zh|874年}}) and is now maintained as an associated shrine of {{ill|Mangai Shrine|de|Mangai Shrine|ja|梛神社|zh|梛神社}} (located in {{ill|Nakagyo Ward|de|Nakagyo Ward|ja|中京区|zh|中京区}} of Kyoto City). For details, see the section "[[Mangai Shrine#Hayai Shrine]]". == == 式外社 == 『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが、同帳に記載の無い神社。 {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=2 | 文献 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=3 | 比定社 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" rowspan=2 | 集成 |- !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 神名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 記事 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 社名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 所在地 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 備考 |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|'''[[大内裏|宮中]]''' |- |'''庭火神'''

[[Category:Shikinaisha top]][[Category:Shikinaisha top]]This is a '''List of Shikinaisha in the Imperial Palace'''. Or the list of shrines in [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which is present in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳}}. On this page we will also cover the {{ill|Shikigeisha|ja|式外社|1=Shikigeisha}} of [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which are shrines that are known to have existed at that time due to other historical records, such as the [[Rikkokushi]], but for some reason were excluded from the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳}}. 式内社の位置}}]] [[File:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|{{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}} 配置図}}]] In the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}}, the Kami Name Register begins by listing 36 shrines in the palace and 3 in the capital. As the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}} was compiled in the mid-{{ill|Heian Period|de|Heian-Zeit|ja|平安時代|zh|平安时代}}, “in the palace” and “in the capital” refer respectively to those within the Heian Palace ({{ill|Heian Capital|de|Heian-Hauptstadt|ja|平安京|zh|Heian Capital}}/{{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|大内裏|zh|Imperial Palace}}) and to those within the city of Heian-kyo. The following explains each enshrined deity. ; Palace Deities (30 major shrines, 6 minor shrines) : This term refers to the deities enshrined within the Imperial Palace of {{ill|Heian Capital|de|Heian-Hauptstadt|ja|平安京|zh|Heian Capital}}, as reported by {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=8}}. The rituals for the 8 Imperial Miko deities were handed down at one of the {{ill|Three Palace Sanctuaries|de|Drei Palastheiligtümer|ja|宮中三殿|zh|三宫殿}} (Shinden), and it is presumed that the worship of the other palace deities was likewise inherited within the “Tenjin-Chigi” section of the Shinden. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}} :; Deities Enshrined in the Western Wing of the {{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}} (21 shrines) ::: These are the deities enshrined at the {{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}}, one of the {{ill|Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|de|Zwei Ämter und Acht Ministerien|ja|二官八省|zh|二官八省}}. The Jingi-kan comprised an Eastern and a Western Wing (Saien); while the Eastern Wing performed administrative duties, the Western Wing handled ritual functions. The deities in the Western Wing, sometimes termed the “Emperor’s Shinto Altar” {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176}}, occupy a key position, although the ancestral deity {{ill|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|zh|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|lt=amaterasu}} is not enshrined there. These gods were served by shrine maidens known as {{ill|Miko|de|Miko|ja|巫女|zh|巫女}}, called “Mikanna.” For each served deity there were 2 chief Mikos (later 3), 1 Zasama Miko, 1 Mikado Miko, and 1 Ikushima Miko. All 21 enshrined deities were designated formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}. ::: Although the Jingi-kan declined and fell into ruin during the medieval period, its continuation is attested until the [[Ōnin]] period (from {{ill|1467th year|de|1467th year|ja|1467年|zh|1467年}} to {{ill|1468th year|de|1468th year|ja|1468年|zh|1468年}}), but by the {{ill|Bunmei Period|de|Bunmei-Ära|ja|文明|zh|文明}} (from {{ill|1469th year|de|1469th year|ja|1469年|zh|1469年}} to {{ill|1486th year|de|1486th year|ja|1486年|zh|1486年}}) it appears to have been completely abolished. In the {{ill|Tenshō Period|de|Tenshō-Ära|ja|天正|zh|天正}} 18th year ({{ill|1590th year|de|1590th year|ja|1590年|zh|1590年}}), eight Shinden were enshrined within the precincts of {{ill|Yoshida Shrine|de|Yoshida Shrine|ja|吉田神社|zh|吉田神社}}, and in the {{ill|Keichō Period|de|Keichō-Ära|ja|慶長|zh|慶长}} 14th year ({{ill|1609th year|de|1609th year|ja|1609年|zh|1609年}}) Yoshida Shrine was designated as the substitute for the Jingi-kan. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|de|Meiji-Restauration|ja|明治維新|zh|明治维新}}, a Shinden enshrining the Eight Gods and Tenjin-Chigi was built within the Imperial Palace, and the ritual practice was maintained; however, since ancient rites had become entirely extinct, the current ceremonies are completely different. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176-201}} :::; {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|lt=Mikamisai-shin|lt_ja=御巫祭神|lt_de=Mikamisai-shin|lt_zh=Mikamisai-shin}} (8 shrines: {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神}}, {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神}}, {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神}}, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}}, {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}, and {{ill|Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神}}). ::::: These 8 deities were served by the chief Miko ({{ill|Oomikanna|de|Oomikanna|ja|大御巫|zh|大御巫}}). According to the personnel regulations set out in the {{ill|Reishūkai|de|Reishūkai|ja|令集解|zh|令集解}}, in the Nara period the chief Miko system consisted of 2 “Wakoku Miko,” but by the Heian period, as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}}, it had expanded to 3—for the Emperor, the {{ill|Empress|de|Kaiserin|ja|中宮|zh|中宫}}, and the {{ill|Crown Prince|de|Kronprinz|ja|東宮|zh|东宫}}. These 8 deities, which include 5 governing souls, one mediating between ruler and subjects ({{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}}), one governing food ({{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}), and one governing language ({{ill|Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神}}), thus serve to pacify the spirit, were enshrined in the {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden}}. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} ({{ill|859th year|de|859th year|ja|859年|zh|859年}}), {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神}}, and {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神}} were promoted to First Rank, while {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神}} was raised to Second Rank. Among these, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}} is said to have passed down a small shrine in the Shuze area of Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Yoshida Shrine|de|Yoshida Shrine|ja|吉田神社|zh|吉田神社}}, is also well known. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=184-187}} :::; {{ill|Zasama-no-kami|de|Zasama-no-kami|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|lt=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_ja=座摩巫祭神|lt_de=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_zh=Zasama-mikanna-shin}} (5 shrines: {{ill|Ikuni-no-kami|de|Ikuni-no-kami|ja|生井神|zh|生井神}}, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社}}, {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神}}, {{ill|Hapihi-no-kami|de|Hapihi-no-kami|ja|波比祇神|zh|波比祇神}}, and {{ill|Asuha-no-kami|de|Asuha-no-kami|ja|阿須波神|zh|阿须波神}}). ::::: These 5 deities were served by a Zasama Miko, who—unlike the other Mikos—was stipulated in the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}} to be the daughter of the {{ill|Tokagenokuzō|de|Tokagenokuzō|ja|闘鶏国造|zh|闘鶏国造|lt=Tokagenokuzō|lt_ja=都下国造|lt_de=Tokagenokuzō|lt_zh=Tokagenokuzō}}. They comprise three deities safeguarding water and two safeguarding the premises, collectively regarded as deities protecting the palace. Their divine Ranks were elevated to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). Among these, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社}} and {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神}} are said to have transmitted a small shrine in Fukunaga-cho, Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社}}, is known in Osaka. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Zasama-shin|de|Zasama-shin|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=187-188}} :::; {{ill|Mikado-no-kami|de|Mikado-no-kami|ja|御門巫祭神|zh|御門巫祭神|lt=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_ja=櫛石窓神|lt_de=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_zh=櫛石窓神}} (8 shrines: 4 for the {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神}} and 4 for the {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神}}) ::::: These 8 deities were served by the Mikado Miko. They enshrined the four gates of the outer perimeter of the {{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|内裏|zh|内裏}}—namely, the East Gate ({{ill|Kenchunmon|de|Kenchunmon|ja|建春門|zh|建春门}}), South Gate ({{ill|Kenreimon|de|Kenreimon|ja|建礼門|zh|建礼门}}), West Gate ({{ill|Gikyuimon|de|Gikyuimon|ja|宜秋門|zh|宜秋门}}), and North Gate ({{ill|Sakuhimon|de|Sakuhimon|ja|朔平門|zh|朔平门}}). One shrine each for {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神}} and {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神}} was enshrined, although the usual festival was held at the Western Wing of the Jingi-kan. There is a theory that because the deities named “Kushiishi Mado-no-kami” and “Toyoshi Mado-no-kami” were enshrined as natural stones—similar to the four guardian deities enshrined as natural stones in the precincts of {{ill|Ise Shrine|de|Ise-Schrein|ja|伊勢神宮|zh|伊势神宫}}—they were in fact enshrined as natural stones at each gate. Their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). An associated shrine, {{ill|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|de|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|ja|櫛石窓神社|zh|櫛石窓神社}}, located in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|de|Hyōgo Prefecture|ja|兵庫県|zh|兵库县}} in {{ill|Tamba Sasayama|de|Tamba Sasayama|ja|丹波篠山市|zh|丹波篠山市}}, is regarded as the original. :::; {{ill|Ikushima-no-kami|de|Ikushima-no-kami|ja|生島神|zh|生島神}} and {{ill|Ashishima-no-kami|de|Ashishima-no-kami|ja|足島神|zh|足島神}} (2 shrines) ::::: These 2 deities were served by the Ikushima Miko. According to the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|de|Kogo Shūi|ja|古語拾遺|zh|古语拾遗}}, they are regarded as the spirits of the nation (the “Great Eight Islands”) and serve as a divine underpinning for the Emperor’s rule. Their divine Ranks were raised to Lower Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). Associated shrines include {{ill|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|de|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|ja|生國魂神社|zh|生国魂神社}} (Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture) and {{ill|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine|de|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine|ja|生島足島神社|zh|生岛足岛神社}} (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture). {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=189-192}} ::: The deities enshrined in the Jingi-kan are described as radiating outward in concentric circles—from the Emperor’s body (served by the Imperial Miko), to the palace (served by the Zasama Miko), to the outer gates (served by the Mikado Miko), and finally to the land (served by the Ikushima Miko). In particular, because associated shrines such as {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社}} and {{ill|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|de|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|ja|生國魂神社|zh|生国魂神社}} remain in Naniwa, it is theorized that the rites once performed at Naniwa Palace continued into the Heian period, with the existence of the {{ill|Ya-shima Festival|de|Ya-shima Festival|ja|八十島祭|zh|八十岛祭}} during imperial enthronements emphasizing Naniwa’s importance. {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=190-192}} ; Deities of the Imperial Household Ministry (3 shrines: Son Shrine and two Kan Shrines) ::: These refer to the deities enshrined within the {{ill|Imperial Household Ministry|de|Kaiserliches Haushaltsministerium|ja|宮内省|zh|宫内省}}, whose exact identities vary – some sources state that the Son deity protects the garden pond, others that the Kan deity wards off epidemics – but in any case they have been enshrined since before the Heian period. All are formal shrines, and their offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}; their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Third Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). For further details, see the article on {{ill|Sonkan Shrine|de|Sonkan Shrine|ja|園韓神社|zh|园韩神社}}. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Court Meals (3 shrines: Mishokutsunushi Shrine, Hurai Shrine, and Koubai Shrine) ::: These deities, under the auspices of the ministry responsible for court meals (the {{ill|Daizen-shoku|de|Daizen-shoku|ja|大膳職|zh|大膳职}}), include {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}, who governs food; {{ill|Hurai Shrine|de|Hurai Shrine|ja|火雷神社|zh|火雷神社}}, who governs water; and {{ill|Koubai Shrine|de|Koubai Shrine|ja|高倍神社|zh|高倍神社}}, associated with earthenware. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859), the divine Rank of {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}} was raised to Lower Third Rank, that of Hurai Shrine to Upper Fifth Rank, and that of Koubai Shrine to Lower Fifth Rank. According to the anecdotal record {{ill|Takahashi Shibun|de|Takahashi Shibun|ja|高橋氏文|zh|高桥氏文}}, see also [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection – Awa Zashinja (Awa Province, Awa District)] and [{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 'Gunsho Ruijū Fifth Volume'] in the National Diet Library Digital Collection, additional details are provided. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Sake Production (4 shrines at O-miyaburushi Shrine; 2 shrines at Sakaden Shrine) ::: These deities, affiliated with the ministry responsible for sake brewing (the {{ill|Zōshūsai|de|Zōshūsai|ja|造酒司|zh|造酒司}}), consist of the O-miyaburushi deity associated with food and sake and two deities governing the water used in brewing. All four O-miyaburushi shrines were formal shrines, with their offerings entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}; in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859) the divine Rank of Sakaden Shrine appears to have been raised to Lower Fifth Rank, and in the 3rd year of Jōgan ({{ill|862nd year|de|862nd year|ja|862年|zh|862年}}) the deities Sakayamitodono Otoko-no-kami and Sakayamitodono Megami were elevated to Upper Fifth Rank. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=32}} ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Water (1 shrine) ::: This is the deity enshrined in the office of the {{ill|Shusui-shi|de|Shusui-shi|ja|主水司|zh|主水司}}, which oversees water and ice procurement—the deity being enshrined at {{ill|Narutai Shrine|de|Narutai Shrine|ja|鳴雷神社|zh|鳴雷神社}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=33}} ; Capital Deities (3 shrines: Taishikoto-no-mikoto, Hisashimitachinomiya, and Hayai Shrine) : These are the deities enshrined within the capital of Heian-kyo, as listed in the Kami Name Register. All three are formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}, and particularly the deities Taishikoto-no-mikoto and Hisashimitachinomiya were also honored at the {{ill|Sounamatsuri|de|Sounamatsuri|ja|相嘗祭|zh|相嘗祭}}. ; {{ill|Ame-no-Osoroshi-no-mikoto|de|Ame-no-Osoroshi-no-mikoto|ja|天児屋命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天児屋命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|lt=Taitatari-no-mikoto|lt_ja=太詔戸命神|lt_de=Taitatari-no-mikoto|lt_zh=Taitatari-no-mikoto}} :: In the Muromachi period, this deity of ritual recitations (prayers) was enshrined to the west. His divine Rank was raised to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859), later to Upper Third Rank. He is now defunct. In the Kami Name Register he appears as the formal shrine in Yamato Province—namely, the “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with Mori Shrine in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|de|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|zh|奈良县}}/{{ill|Tenri City|de|Tenri City|ja|天理市|zh|天理市}}) and in Tsushima Province as “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with {{ill|Taishikoto Shrine|de|Taishikoto Shrine|ja|太祝詞神社|zh|太祝詞神社}} in {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|de|Nagasaki Prefecture|ja|長崎県|zh|长崎县}}/{{ill|Tsushima City|de|Tsushima City|ja|対馬市|zh|对马市}}); these are regarded as his original enclosures. ; {{ill|Kushimachinomiya|de|Kushimachinomiya|ja|櫛真智命|zh|櫛真智命|lt=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_ja=久慈真智命神|lt_de=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_zh=Hisashimitachinomiya}} :: Enshrined to the west of the Shijōbōmon area, this divinized deity of divination was elevated to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859) and is now defunct. According to the Kami Name Register, his original shrine is the “Tenkōzan Zari Kushinomiya Shrine” in Yamato Province (with candidate shrines in [[Kashihara City]] of Nara Prefecture, including Tenkōzan Shrine and Kuninotokotachi Shrine) and is considered his original. ; {{ill|Hayai Shrine|de|Hayai Shrine|ja|隼神社|zh|隼神社}} :: Enshrined within the Shujakuin of the Later Palace, this deity was raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the sixteenth year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} ({{ill|874th year|de|874th year|ja|874年|zh|874年}}) and is now maintained as an associated shrine of {{ill|Mangai Shrine|de|Mangai Shrine|ja|梛神社|zh|梛神社}} (located in {{ill|Nakagyo Ward|de|Nakagyo Ward|ja|中京区|zh|中京区}} of Kyoto City). For details, see the section "[[Mangai Shrine#Hayai Shrine]]". == == 式外社 == 『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが、同帳に記載の無い神社。 {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=2 | 文献 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=3 | 比定社 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" rowspan=2 | 集成 |- !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 神名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 記事 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 社名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 所在地 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 備考 |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|'''[[大内裏|宮中]]''' |- |'''庭火神'''

'''宮中・京中の式内社一覧'''（きゅうちゅう・きょうちゅうのしきないしゃいちらん）は、『[[延喜式]]』第9巻・第10巻「神名帳上下」（[[延喜式神名帳]]）に記載のある[[神社]]、いわゆる「[[式内社]]」およびその[[論社]]のうち、[[大内裏|宮中]]および[[平安京|京中]]に分類されている神社の一覧。 また『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが同帳に記載の無い神社、いわゆる「[[式外社]]」についても付記する。 == 式内社 == 『延喜式』神名帳では、宮中に36座（大30座・小6座）、京中に大3座を記載。 {{式内社一覧/凡例}} {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; font-size:85%" align="left" ! style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=5 | 神名帳 ! style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=3 | 比定社 ! style="background:#a0f0a0" rowspan=2 | 集成 |- style="white-space:nowrap;" ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.6em; padding-left:2.6em;" colspan=2 | 社名 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.1em; padding-left:2.1em;" | 読み ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.1em; padding-left:2.1em;" | 格 ! style="background:#a0f0a0;" | 付記 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.6em; padding-left:2.6em;" | 社名 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.1em; padding-left:2.1em;" | 所在地 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.3em; padding-left:2.3em;" | 備考 |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|'''[[大内裏|宮中]]''' |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#ccffcc"|'''[[神祇官]]西院坐御巫等祭神''' 23座（並大） |- |colspan="2"|'''[[八神殿|御巫祭神]] 八座'''||||並大||月次新嘗

式内社の位置}}]] [[ファイル:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|[[神祇官]]配置図}}]] 『延喜式』神名帳では、その冒頭に宮中36座・京中3座の神々を記載する。『延喜式』は[[平安時代]]中期の成立になるため、宮中・京中とはそれぞれ平安宮（[[平安京]][[大内裏]]）中・平安京中を意味する。以下、各祭神について解説する。 ; 宮中神（大30座、小6座） : [[平安京]]の[[大内裏]]中に祀られた神々を指す{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=8}}。御巫祭神8座の祭祀は皇居内に建てられた[[宮中三殿|神殿]]（[[宮中三殿]]の1つ）に継承されるが、他の宮中諸神の祭祀も神殿の「天神地祇」中に継承されたと推測される。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=28-29}} :; 神祇官西院坐御巫等祭神（大21座） ::: [[神祇官]]（[[二官八省]]の1つ）で祀られた神々。神祇官は東院・西院（斎院）からなるが、東院が事務機能を、西院が祭祀機能を果たした。その西院に祀られる神々は「天皇の神棚」{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=176}}とも言うべき位置づけにあるが、皇祖神である[[天照大神|アマテラス]]は祀られていない。諸神は「御巫（みかんなぎ）」と称される童女の[[巫女]]によって奉斎された。この御巫には、各奉仕神に応じて大御巫2人（のち3人）・座摩巫1人・御門巫1人・生島巫1人があった。奉斎される21座はいずれも式内大社で、[[月次祭]]・[[新嘗祭]]では幣帛に預かった。 ::: 神祇官は中世には衰退・荒廃するも、[[応仁]]年間（[[1467年]]-[[1468年]]）までの継続は確認されるが、[[文明 (日本)|文明]]年間（[[1469年]]-[[1486年]]）頃には完全に廃絶する。[[天正]]18年（[[1590年]]）に[[吉田神社]]境内に八神殿が祀られ、[[慶長]]14年（[[1609年]]）には吉田神社をもって神祇官代と制定。[[明治維新]]後は皇居内に八神と天神地祇を祀る神殿が建てられて祭祀が継承されているが、古代祭祀は完全に消滅したため内容は全く異なるものとなっている。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=176-201}} :::; [[八神殿|御巫祭神]]（大8座：[[神産日神]]・[[高御産日神]]・玉積産日神・[[生産日神]]・足産日神・[[大宮売神]]・[[御食津神]]・[[事代主神]]） ::::: 大御巫（おおみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された8神。大御巫は『[[令集解]]』職員令によると奈良時代には「倭国巫」2人からなったが、『延喜式』によると平安時代には天皇・[[中宮]]・[[東宮]]のため3人からなった。霊魂を司る5神、君臣の間を取り持つ大宮売神、食物を司る御食津神、言葉を司る事代主神からなり、魂を身体に鎮めるための鎮魂8神とされる。神祇官西院中の[[八神殿]]に祀られ、[[神階]]は[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]元年（[[859年]]）に神産日神・高御産日神・玉積産日神・足産日神は正一位、生産日神は従一位に昇った。8神のうち大宮売神は京都市上京区主税町に小祠を伝える。また関連社として[[大宮売神社]]（[[京都府]][[京丹後市]]）が知られる。詳細は「[[八神殿]]」を参照。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=184-187}} :::; [[座摩神|座摩巫祭神]]（大5座：生井神・福井神・綱長井神・波比祇神・阿須波神） ::::: 座摩巫（いかすりのみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された5神。座摩巫だけは他の御巫と異なり、『延喜式』において[[闘鶏国造|都下国造]]の娘とすると規定されている。井水守護の3神、敷地守護の2神からなり、総じて宮所守護の神々とされる。神階は貞観元年（859年）に従四位上に昇った。5神のうち福井神・綱長井神は[[福長神社]]（京都市上京区福長町）に小祠を伝える。関連社として[[坐摩神社]]（[[大阪府]][[大阪市]]）が知られる。詳細は「[[座摩神]]」を参照。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=187-188}} :::; [[天石門別神|御門巫祭神]]（大8座：[[櫛石窓神]]四面門各一座・[[豊石窓神]]四面門各一座） ::::: 御門巫（みかどのみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された8神。[[内裏]]外郭の4面の門、すなわち建春門（東）・建礼門（南）・宜秋門（西）・朔平門（北）を祀る神々で、櫛石窓神・豊石窓神が各1座ずつ奉斎されたが、平常の祭りは神祇官西院で行なわれたとされる。「櫛石窓神」「豊石窓神」という神名や、[[伊勢神宮]]の宮域守護の四至神が自然石として祀られていることから、各門に自然石として祀られたとする説がある。神階は貞観元年（859年）に従四位上。関連社として知られる[[櫛石窓神社]]（[[兵庫県]][[丹波篠山市]]）が元社になるという説がある。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=26-27}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=188-189}} :::; 生島巫祭神（大2座：生島神・足島神） ::::: 生島巫（いくしまのみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された2神。『[[古語拾遺]]』によれば、大八洲すなわち国土の霊たる神々とされる。天皇による国土支配の裏付けになる神霊である。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正四位下に昇った。関連社として[[生國魂神社]]（大阪府大阪市）、[[生島足島神社]]（[[長野県]][[上田市]]）が知られる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=189-192}} ::: 以上の神祇官に祀られる神々は、天皇の身体（御巫祭神）、天皇の住居（座摩巫祭神）、住居外側の門（御門巫祭神）、そして国土（生島巫祭神）と同心円状に外へ拡大するように記載されている。また特に座摩神と生島神については、関連社として難波に[[坐摩神社]]と[[生國魂神社]]が残ることから、[[難波宮]]での祭祀が平安京の時代まで継承されたとする説があり、天皇即位の際に難波で代々行われた[[八十島祭]]の存在も併せて難波が重視された様子が指摘される。{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=190-192}} :; 宮内省坐神（大3座：園神社・韓神社二座） ::: [[宮内省]]（二官八省の1つ）に祀られた神々。園神は園池を守る神であるとも、園韓神をして疫病を防ぐ神であるとも、園韓神とも平安京以前から鎮座した神であるともいわれるが、明らかではない。いずれも式内名神大社で、月次祭・新嘗祭では幣帛に預かった。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正三位に昇った。詳細は「[[園韓神社]]」を参照。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=24-25}} :; 大膳職坐神（小3座：御食津神社・火雷神社・高倍神社） ::: 宮内省に属し、饗膳を司る[[大膳職]]に祀られた神々。食物を司る御食津神、水を司る火雷神、土器を司る醤院の高倍神（高瓶神の意か）からなる。貞観元年（859年）に御食津神の神階は従三位に、火雷神は従五位上に、高部神（高倍神）は従五位下に昇った{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=31}}。『[[高橋氏文]]』逸文『本朝月令』6月朔日内膳司供忌火御飯事所引『高橋氏文』逸文（[http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html 神道・神社史料集成-安房坐神社（安房国安房郡）]参照、[{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 『群書類従 第五輯』]<国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション>56-57コマ参照）。によれば、[[上総国]]安房神社は『延喜式』神名帳において安房国の所在であるが、上総国とする『高橋氏文』の記載は、『高橋氏文』の成立当時に[[安房国]]が上総国のうちに含まれていたことによる。の安房大神（現在の[[安房神社]]（[[千葉県]][[館山市]]）に比定）がその御食津神（文中では御食都神と表記）であるという『千葉県の歴史 通史編 古代2（県史シリーズ2）』 千葉県、2001年、pp. 604-607。。 :; 造酒司坐神（大4座：大宮売神社四座、小2座：酒殿神社二座） ::: 宮内省に属し、酒等の醸造を司る[[造酒司]]に祀られた神々。御食・造酒に関係する大宮売神、酒水を司る2神からなる。大宮売神4座はいずれも式内大社で、月次祭・新嘗祭では幣帛に預かった。貞観元年（859年）に酒殿神の神階が従五位下に昇ったと見えるほか、貞観3年（[[862年]]）に酒弥豆男神・酒弥豆女神は従五位上に昇った。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=32}} :; 主水司坐神（小1座：鳴雷神社） ::: 宮内省に属し、水・氷の調達等を司る[[主水司]]に祀られた神。水を司る鳴雷神からなる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=33}} ; 京中神（大3座：太詔戸命神・久慈真智命神・隼神社） : 平安京中に祀られた神々を指す{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=8}}。神名帳には3座が載せられている。いずれも式内大社で、月次祭・新嘗祭では幣帛に預かったほか、太詔戸命神・久慈真智命神は特に[[相嘗祭]]でも幣帛に預かった。 :; [[天児屋命|太詔戸命神]] :: 室町の西に祀られた[[祝詞]]の神。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正五位下に昇った（のち正三位）。現在は廃絶。神名帳では[[大和国]][[添上郡]]に式内大社「太祝詞神社」（現在の森神社（[[奈良県]][[天理市]]）に比定）、[[対馬国]][[下県郡]]に式内名神大社「太祝詞神社」（現在の[[太祝詞神社]]（[[長崎県]][[対馬市]]）に比定）が見え、これらが元社になると見られる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=34-36}} :; [[櫛真智命|久慈真智命神]] :: 四条坊門坊域の西に祀られた[[卜占]]の神。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正五位下に昇った。現在は廃絶。神名帳では大和国[[十市郡]]に式内大社「天香山坐櫛真命神社」（論社に奈良県[[橿原市]]の天香山神社と国常立神社）と見え、これが元社になると見られる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=34-36}} :; 隼神 :: 後院の[[朱雀院]]の院内に祀られた神。神階は貞観16年（[[874年]]）に従四位上に昇った。現在は[[梛神社]]（京都市[[中京区]]壬生梛ノ宮町）の境内社として継承されている。詳細は「[[梛神社#隼神社]]」を参照。 == 式外社 == {{節stub}} 『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが、同帳に記載の無い神社。 {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; '''宮中・京中の式内社一覧'''（きゅうちゅう・きょうちゅうのしきないしゃいちらん）は、『[[延喜式]]』第9巻・第10巻「神名帳上下」（[[延喜式神名帳]]）に記載のある[[神社]]、いわゆる「[[式内社]]」およびその[[論社]]のうち、[[大内裏|宮中]]および[[平安京|京中]]に分類されている神社の一覧。 また『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが同帳に記載の無い神社、いわゆる「[[式外社]]」についても付記する。 == 式内社 == 『延喜式』神名帳では、宮中に36座（大30座・小6座）、京中に大3座を記載。 {{式内社一覧/凡例}} {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; font-size:85%" align="left" ! style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=5 | 神名帳 ! style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=3 | 比定社 ! style="background:#a0f0a0" rowspan=2 | 集成 |- style="white-space:nowrap;" ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.6em; padding-left:2.6em;" colspan=2 | 社名 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.1em; padding-left:2.1em;" | 読み ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.1em; padding-left:2.1em;" | 格 ! style="background:#a0f0a0;" | 付記 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.6em; padding-left:2.6em;" | 社名 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.1em; padding-left:2.1em;" | 所在地 ! style="background:#a0f0a0; padding-right:2.3em; padding-left:2.3em;" | 備考 |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|'''[[大内裏|宮中]]''' |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#ccffcc"|'''[[神祇官]]西院坐御巫等祭神''' 23座（並大） |- |colspan="2"|'''[[八神殿|御巫祭神]] 八座'''||||並大||月次新嘗

式内社の位置}}]] [[ファイル:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|[[神祇官]]配置図}}]] 『延喜式』神名帳では、その冒頭に宮中36座・京中3座の神々を記載する。『延喜式』は[[平安時代]]中期の成立になるため、宮中・京中とはそれぞれ平安宮（[[平安京]][[大内裏]]）中・平安京中を意味する。以下、各祭神について解説する。 ; 宮中神（大30座、小6座） : [[平安京]]の[[大内裏]]中に祀られた神々を指す{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=8}}。御巫祭神8座の祭祀は皇居内に建てられた[[宮中三殿|神殿]]（[[宮中三殿]]の1つ）に継承されるが、他の宮中諸神の祭祀も神殿の「天神地祇」中に継承されたと推測される。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=28-29}} :; 神祇官西院坐御巫等祭神（大21座） ::: [[神祇官]]（[[二官八省]]の1つ）で祀られた神々。神祇官は東院・西院（斎院）からなるが、東院が事務機能を、西院が祭祀機能を果たした。その西院に祀られる神々は「天皇の神棚」{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=176}}とも言うべき位置づけにあるが、皇祖神である[[天照大神|アマテラス]]は祀られていない。諸神は「御巫（みかんなぎ）」と称される童女の[[巫女]]によって奉斎された。この御巫には、各奉仕神に応じて大御巫2人（のち3人）・座摩巫1人・御門巫1人・生島巫1人があった。奉斎される21座はいずれも式内大社で、[[月次祭]]・[[新嘗祭]]では幣帛に預かった。 ::: 神祇官は中世には衰退・荒廃するも、[[応仁]]年間（[[1467年]]-[[1468年]]）までの継続は確認されるが、[[文明 (日本)|文明]]年間（[[1469年]]-[[1486年]]）頃には完全に廃絶する。[[天正]]18年（[[1590年]]）に[[吉田神社]]境内に八神殿が祀られ、[[慶長]]14年（[[1609年]]）には吉田神社をもって神祇官代と制定。[[明治維新]]後は皇居内に八神と天神地祇を祀る神殿が建てられて祭祀が継承されているが、古代祭祀は完全に消滅したため内容は全く異なるものとなっている。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=176-201}} :::; [[八神殿|御巫祭神]]（大8座：[[神産日神]]・[[高御産日神]]・玉積産日神・[[生産日神]]・足産日神・[[大宮売神]]・[[御食津神]]・[[事代主神]]） ::::: 大御巫（おおみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された8神。大御巫は『[[令集解]]』職員令によると奈良時代には「倭国巫」2人からなったが、『延喜式』によると平安時代には天皇・[[中宮]]・[[東宮]]のため3人からなった。霊魂を司る5神、君臣の間を取り持つ大宮売神、食物を司る御食津神、言葉を司る事代主神からなり、魂を身体に鎮めるための鎮魂8神とされる。神祇官西院中の[[八神殿]]に祀られ、[[神階]]は[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]元年（[[859年]]）に神産日神・高御産日神・玉積産日神・足産日神は正一位、生産日神は従一位に昇った。8神のうち大宮売神は京都市上京区主税町に小祠を伝える。また関連社として[[大宮売神社]]（[[京都府]][[京丹後市]]）が知られる。詳細は「[[八神殿]]」を参照。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=184-187}} :::; [[座摩神|座摩巫祭神]]（大5座：生井神・福井神・綱長井神・波比祇神・阿須波神） ::::: 座摩巫（いかすりのみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された5神。座摩巫だけは他の御巫と異なり、『延喜式』において[[闘鶏国造|都下国造]]の娘とすると規定されている。井水守護の3神、敷地守護の2神からなり、総じて宮所守護の神々とされる。神階は貞観元年（859年）に従四位上に昇った。5神のうち福井神・綱長井神は[[福長神社]]（京都市上京区福長町）に小祠を伝える。関連社として[[坐摩神社]]（[[大阪府]][[大阪市]]）が知られる。詳細は「[[座摩神]]」を参照。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=187-188}} :::; [[天石門別神|御門巫祭神]]（大8座：[[櫛石窓神]]四面門各一座・[[豊石窓神]]四面門各一座） ::::: 御門巫（みかどのみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された8神。[[内裏]]外郭の4面の門、すなわち建春門（東）・建礼門（南）・宜秋門（西）・朔平門（北）を祀る神々で、櫛石窓神・豊石窓神が各1座ずつ奉斎されたが、平常の祭りは神祇官西院で行なわれたとされる。「櫛石窓神」「豊石窓神」という神名や、[[伊勢神宮]]の宮域守護の四至神が自然石として祀られていることから、各門に自然石として祀られたとする説がある。神階は貞観元年（859年）に従四位上。関連社として知られる[[櫛石窓神社]]（[[兵庫県]][[丹波篠山市]]）が元社になるという説がある。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=26-27}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=188-189}} :::; 生島巫祭神（大2座：生島神・足島神） ::::: 生島巫（いくしまのみかんなぎ）によって奉斎された2神。『[[古語拾遺]]』によれば、大八洲すなわち国土の霊たる神々とされる。天皇による国土支配の裏付けになる神霊である。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正四位下に昇った。関連社として[[生國魂神社]]（大阪府大阪市）、[[生島足島神社]]（[[長野県]][[上田市]]）が知られる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=189-192}} ::: 以上の神祇官に祀られる神々は、天皇の身体（御巫祭神）、天皇の住居（座摩巫祭神）、住居外側の門（御門巫祭神）、そして国土（生島巫祭神）と同心円状に外へ拡大するように記載されている。また特に座摩神と生島神については、関連社として難波に[[坐摩神社]]と[[生國魂神社]]が残ることから、[[難波宮]]での祭祀が平安京の時代まで継承されたとする説があり、天皇即位の際に難波で代々行われた[[八十島祭]]の存在も併せて難波が重視された様子が指摘される。{{Sfn|神社の古代史|2011年|p=190-192}} :; 宮内省坐神（大3座：園神社・韓神社二座） ::: [[宮内省]]（二官八省の1つ）に祀られた神々。園神は園池を守る神であるとも、園韓神をして疫病を防ぐ神であるとも、園韓神とも平安京以前から鎮座した神であるともいわれるが、明らかではない。いずれも式内名神大社で、月次祭・新嘗祭では幣帛に預かった。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正三位に昇った。詳細は「[[園韓神社]]」を参照。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|pp=24-25}} :; 大膳職坐神（小3座：御食津神社・火雷神社・高倍神社） ::: 宮内省に属し、饗膳を司る[[大膳職]]に祀られた神々。食物を司る御食津神、水を司る火雷神、土器を司る醤院の高倍神（高瓶神の意か）からなる。貞観元年（859年）に御食津神の神階は従三位に、火雷神は従五位上に、高部神（高倍神）は従五位下に昇った{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=31}}。『[[高橋氏文]]』逸文『本朝月令』6月朔日内膳司供忌火御飯事所引『高橋氏文』逸文（[http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html 神道・神社史料集成-安房坐神社（安房国安房郡）]参照、[{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 『群書類従 第五輯』]<国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション>56-57コマ参照）。によれば、[[上総国]]安房神社は『延喜式』神名帳において安房国の所在であるが、上総国とする『高橋氏文』の記載は、『高橋氏文』の成立当時に[[安房国]]が上総国のうちに含まれていたことによる。の安房大神（現在の[[安房神社]]（[[千葉県]][[館山市]]）に比定）がその御食津神（文中では御食都神と表記）であるという『千葉県の歴史 通史編 古代2（県史シリーズ2）』 千葉県、2001年、pp. 604-607。。 :; 造酒司坐神（大4座：大宮売神社四座、小2座：酒殿神社二座） ::: 宮内省に属し、酒等の醸造を司る[[造酒司]]に祀られた神々。御食・造酒に関係する大宮売神、酒水を司る2神からなる。大宮売神4座はいずれも式内大社で、月次祭・新嘗祭では幣帛に預かった。貞観元年（859年）に酒殿神の神階が従五位下に昇ったと見えるほか、貞観3年（[[862年]]）に酒弥豆男神・酒弥豆女神は従五位上に昇った。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=32}} :; 主水司坐神（小1座：鳴雷神社） ::: 宮内省に属し、水・氷の調達等を司る[[主水司]]に祀られた神。水を司る鳴雷神からなる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=33}} ; 京中神（大3座：太詔戸命神・久慈真智命神・隼神社） : 平安京中に祀られた神々を指す{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=8}}。神名帳には3座が載せられている。いずれも式内大社で、月次祭・新嘗祭では幣帛に預かったほか、太詔戸命神・久慈真智命神は特に[[相嘗祭]]でも幣帛に預かった。 :; [[天児屋命|太詔戸命神]] :: 室町の西に祀られた[[祝詞]]の神。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正五位下に昇った（のち正三位）。現在は廃絶。神名帳では[[大和国]][[添上郡]]に式内大社「太祝詞神社」（現在の森神社（[[奈良県]][[天理市]]）に比定）、[[対馬国]][[下県郡]]に式内名神大社「太祝詞神社」（現在の[[太祝詞神社]]（[[長崎県]][[対馬市]]）に比定）が見え、これらが元社になると見られる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=34-36}} :; [[櫛真智命|久慈真智命神]] :: 四条坊門坊域の西に祀られた[[卜占]]の神。神階は貞観元年（859年）に正五位下に昇った。現在は廃絶。神名帳では大和国[[十市郡]]に式内大社「天香山坐櫛真命神社」（論社に奈良県[[橿原市]]の天香山神社と国常立神社）と見え、これが元社になると見られる。{{Sfn|式内社調査報告|1979年|p=34-36}} :; 隼神 :: 後院の[[朱雀院]]の院内に祀られた神。神階は貞観16年（[[874年]]）に従四位上に昇った。現在は[[梛神社]]（京都市[[中京区]]壬生梛ノ宮町）の境内社として継承されている。詳細は「[[梛神社#隼神社]]」を参照。 == 式外社 == {{節stub}} 『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが、同帳に記載の無い神社。 {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; [[Category:Shikinaisha top]][[Category:Shikinaisha top]]This is a '''List of Shikinaisha in the Imperial Palace'''. Or the list of shrines in [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which is present in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳}}. On this page we will also cover the {{ill|Shikigeisha|ja|式外社|1=Shikigeisha}} of [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which are shrines that are known to have existed at that time due to other historical records, such as the [[Rikkokushi]], but for some reason were excluded from the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳}}. naruikatsuchi||Shikinai Shosha||||colspan=2|（[[Three Palace Sanctuaries]], inherited by the Shinden?）|| || |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|[[Heian-kyō]] |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#ccffcc"|'''左京二条坐神''' 2座（並大） |- |colspan="2"|'''太詔戸命神'''||futonotonomikotono||Shikinai Taisha||月次相嘗新嘗||colspan=2|（廃絶）||||[http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=1401] |- |colspan="2"|'''久慈真智命神'''||kushimachinomikotono||Shikinai Taisha||月次相嘗新嘗||colspan=2|（廃絶）||||[http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=1402] |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#ccffcc"|'''左京四条坐神''' 1座（大） |- |colspan="2"|'''隼神社'''||hayafusano||Shikinai Taisha||月次新嘗||[[梛神社#隼神社|隼神社]]||京都府京都市[[中京区]]壬生梛no宮町||[[梛神社]]境内社||[http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=1901] |}{{-}} == Explanation == [[File:宮中の式内社位置.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|{{ill|Heian Capital|de|Heian-Hauptstadt|ja|平安京|zh|Heian Capital}} {{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|大内裏|zh|Imperial Palace}} における
式内社の位置}}]] [[File:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|{{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}} 配置図}}]] In the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}}, the Kami Name Register begins by listing 36 shrines in the palace and 3 in the capital. As the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}} was compiled in the mid-{{ill|Heian Period|de|Heian-Zeit|ja|平安時代|zh|平安时代}}, “in the palace” and “in the capital” refer respectively to those within the Heian Palace ({{ill|Heian Capital|de|Heian-Hauptstadt|ja|平安京|zh|Heian Capital}}/{{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|大内裏|zh|Imperial Palace}}) and to those within the city of Heian-kyo. The following explains each enshrined deity. ; Palace Deities (30 major shrines, 6 minor shrines) : This term refers to the deities enshrined within the Imperial Palace of {{ill|Heian Capital|de|Heian-Hauptstadt|ja|平安京|zh|Heian Capital}}, as reported by {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=8}}. The rituals for the 8 Imperial Miko deities were handed down at one of the {{ill|Three Palace Sanctuaries|de|Drei Palastheiligtümer|ja|宮中三殿|zh|三宫殿}} (Shinden), and it is presumed that the worship of the other palace deities was likewise inherited within the “Tenjin-Chigi” section of the Shinden. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}} :; Deities Enshrined in the Western Wing of the {{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}} (21 shrines) ::: These are the deities enshrined at the {{ill|Jingi-kan|de|Jingi-kan|ja|神祇官|zh|神祇官}}, one of the {{ill|Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|de|Zwei Ämter und Acht Ministerien|ja|二官八省|zh|二官八省}}. The Jingi-kan comprised an Eastern and a Western Wing (Saien); while the Eastern Wing performed administrative duties, the Western Wing handled ritual functions. The deities in the Western Wing, sometimes termed the “Emperor’s Shinto Altar” {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176}}, occupy a key position, although the ancestral deity {{ill|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|zh|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|lt=amaterasu}} is not enshrined there. These gods were served by shrine maidens known as {{ill|Miko|de|Miko|ja|巫女|zh|巫女}}, called “Mikanna.” For each served deity there were 2 chief Mikos (later 3), 1 Zasama Miko, 1 Mikado Miko, and 1 Ikushima Miko. All 21 enshrined deities were designated formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}. ::: Although the Jingi-kan declined and fell into ruin during the medieval period, its continuation is attested until the [[Ōnin]] period (from {{ill|1467th year|de|1467th year|ja|1467年|zh|1467年}} to {{ill|1468th year|de|1468th year|ja|1468年|zh|1468年}}), but by the {{ill|Bunmei Period|de|Bunmei-Ära|ja|文明|zh|文明}} (from {{ill|1469th year|de|1469th year|ja|1469年|zh|1469年}} to {{ill|1486th year|de|1486th year|ja|1486年|zh|1486年}}) it appears to have been completely abolished. In the {{ill|Tenshō Period|de|Tenshō-Ära|ja|天正|zh|天正}} 18th year ({{ill|1590th year|de|1590th year|ja|1590年|zh|1590年}}), eight Shinden were enshrined within the precincts of {{ill|Yoshida Shrine|de|Yoshida Shrine|ja|吉田神社|zh|吉田神社}}, and in the {{ill|Keichō Period|de|Keichō-Ära|ja|慶長|zh|慶长}} 14th year ({{ill|1609th year|de|1609th year|ja|1609年|zh|1609年}}) Yoshida Shrine was designated as the substitute for the Jingi-kan. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|de|Meiji-Restauration|ja|明治維新|zh|明治维新}}, a Shinden enshrining the Eight Gods and Tenjin-Chigi was built within the Imperial Palace, and the ritual practice was maintained; however, since ancient rites had become entirely extinct, the current ceremonies are completely different. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176-201}} :::; {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|lt=Mikamisai-shin|lt_ja=御巫祭神|lt_de=Mikamisai-shin|lt_zh=Mikamisai-shin}} (8 shrines: {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神}}, {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神}}, {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神}}, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}}, {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}, and {{ill|Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神}}). ::::: These 8 deities were served by the chief Miko ({{ill|Oomikanna|de|Oomikanna|ja|大御巫|zh|大御巫}}). According to the personnel regulations set out in the {{ill|Reishūkai|de|Reishūkai|ja|令集解|zh|令集解}}, in the Nara period the chief Miko system consisted of 2 “Wakoku Miko,” but by the Heian period, as recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}}, it had expanded to 3—for the Emperor, the {{ill|Empress|de|Kaiserin|ja|中宮|zh|中宫}}, and the {{ill|Crown Prince|de|Kronprinz|ja|東宮|zh|东宫}}. These 8 deities, which include 5 governing souls, one mediating between ruler and subjects ({{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}}), one governing food ({{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}), and one governing language ({{ill|Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神}}), thus serve to pacify the spirit, were enshrined in the {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden}}. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} ({{ill|859th year|de|859th year|ja|859年|zh|859年}}), {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神}}, and {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神}} were promoted to First Rank, while {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神}} was raised to Second Rank. Among these, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神}} is said to have passed down a small shrine in the Shuze area of Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Yoshida Shrine|de|Yoshida Shrine|ja|吉田神社|zh|吉田神社}}, is also well known. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=184-187}} :::; {{ill|Zasama-no-kami|de|Zasama-no-kami|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|lt=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_ja=座摩巫祭神|lt_de=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_zh=Zasama-mikanna-shin}} (5 shrines: {{ill|Ikuni-no-kami|de|Ikuni-no-kami|ja|生井神|zh|生井神}}, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社}}, {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神}}, {{ill|Hapihi-no-kami|de|Hapihi-no-kami|ja|波比祇神|zh|波比祇神}}, and {{ill|Asuha-no-kami|de|Asuha-no-kami|ja|阿須波神|zh|阿须波神}}). ::::: These 5 deities were served by a Zasama Miko, who—unlike the other Mikos—was stipulated in the {{ill|Engishiki|de|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|zh|Engishiki}} to be the daughter of the {{ill|Tokagenokuzō|de|Tokagenokuzō|ja|闘鶏国造|zh|闘鶏国造|lt=Tokagenokuzō|lt_ja=都下国造|lt_de=Tokagenokuzō|lt_zh=Tokagenokuzō}}. They comprise three deities safeguarding water and two safeguarding the premises, collectively regarded as deities protecting the palace. Their divine Ranks were elevated to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). Among these, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社}} and {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神}} are said to have transmitted a small shrine in Fukunaga-cho, Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社}}, is known in Osaka. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Zasama-shin|de|Zasama-shin|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=187-188}} :::; {{ill|Mikado-no-kami|de|Mikado-no-kami|ja|御門巫祭神|zh|御門巫祭神|lt=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_ja=櫛石窓神|lt_de=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_zh=櫛石窓神}} (8 shrines: 4 for the {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神}} and 4 for the {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神}}) ::::: These 8 deities were served by the Mikado Miko. They enshrined the four gates of the outer perimeter of the {{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|内裏|zh|内裏}}—namely, the East Gate ({{ill|Kenchunmon|de|Kenchunmon|ja|建春門|zh|建春门}}), South Gate ({{ill|Kenreimon|de|Kenreimon|ja|建礼門|zh|建礼门}}), West Gate ({{ill|Gikyuimon|de|Gikyuimon|ja|宜秋門|zh|宜秋门}}), and North Gate ({{ill|Sakuhimon|de|Sakuhimon|ja|朔平門|zh|朔平门}}). One shrine each for {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神}} and {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神}} was enshrined, although the usual festival was held at the Western Wing of the Jingi-kan. There is a theory that because the deities named “Kushiishi Mado-no-kami” and “Toyoshi Mado-no-kami” were enshrined as natural stones—similar to the four guardian deities enshrined as natural stones in the precincts of {{ill|Ise Shrine|de|Ise-Schrein|ja|伊勢神宮|zh|伊势神宫}}—they were in fact enshrined as natural stones at each gate. Their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). An associated shrine, {{ill|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|de|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|ja|櫛石窓神社|zh|櫛石窓神社}}, located in {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|de|Hyōgo Prefecture|ja|兵庫県|zh|兵库县}} in {{ill|Tamba Sasayama|de|Tamba Sasayama|ja|丹波篠山市|zh|丹波篠山市}}, is regarded as the original. :::; {{ill|Ikushima-no-kami|de|Ikushima-no-kami|ja|生島神|zh|生島神}} and {{ill|Ashishima-no-kami|de|Ashishima-no-kami|ja|足島神|zh|足島神}} (2 shrines) ::::: These 2 deities were served by the Ikushima Miko. According to the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|de|Kogo Shūi|ja|古語拾遺|zh|古语拾遗}}, they are regarded as the spirits of the nation (the “Great Eight Islands”) and serve as a divine underpinning for the Emperor’s rule. Their divine Ranks were raised to Lower Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). Associated shrines include {{ill|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|de|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|ja|生國魂神社|zh|生国魂神社}} (Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture) and {{ill|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine|de|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine|ja|生島足島神社|zh|生岛足岛神社}} (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture). {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=189-192}} ::: The deities enshrined in the Jingi-kan are described as radiating outward in concentric circles—from the Emperor’s body (served by the Imperial Miko), to the palace (served by the Zasama Miko), to the outer gates (served by the Mikado Miko), and finally to the land (served by the Ikushima Miko). In particular, because associated shrines such as {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社}} and {{ill|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|de|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine|ja|生國魂神社|zh|生国魂神社}} remain in Naniwa, it is theorized that the rites once performed at Naniwa Palace continued into the Heian period, with the existence of the {{ill|Ya-shima Festival|de|Ya-shima Festival|ja|八十島祭|zh|八十岛祭}} during imperial enthronements emphasizing Naniwa’s importance. {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=190-192}} ; Deities of the Imperial Household Ministry (3 shrines: Son Shrine and two Kan Shrines) ::: These refer to the deities enshrined within the {{ill|Imperial Household Ministry|de|Kaiserliches Haushaltsministerium|ja|宮内省|zh|宫内省}}, whose exact identities vary – some sources state that the Son deity protects the garden pond, others that the Kan deity wards off epidemics – but in any case they have been enshrined since before the Heian period. All are formal shrines, and their offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}; their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Third Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859). For further details, see the article on {{ill|Sonkan Shrine|de|Sonkan Shrine|ja|園韓神社|zh|园韩神社}}. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Court Meals (3 shrines: Mishokutsunushi Shrine, Hurai Shrine, and Koubai Shrine) ::: These deities, under the auspices of the ministry responsible for court meals (the {{ill|Daizen-shoku|de|Daizen-shoku|ja|大膳職|zh|大膳职}}), include {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}}, who governs food; {{ill|Hurai Shrine|de|Hurai Shrine|ja|火雷神社|zh|火雷神社}}, who governs water; and {{ill|Koubai Shrine|de|Koubai Shrine|ja|高倍神社|zh|高倍神社}}, associated with earthenware. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859), the divine Rank of {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神}} was raised to Lower Third Rank, that of Hurai Shrine to Upper Fifth Rank, and that of Koubai Shrine to Lower Fifth Rank. According to the anecdotal record {{ill|Takahashi Shibun|de|Takahashi Shibun|ja|高橋氏文|zh|高桥氏文}}, see also [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection – Awa Zashinja (Awa Province, Awa District)] and [{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 'Gunsho Ruijū Fifth Volume'] in the National Diet Library Digital Collection, additional details are provided. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Sake Production (4 shrines at O-miyaburushi Shrine; 2 shrines at Sakaden Shrine) ::: These deities, affiliated with the ministry responsible for sake brewing (the {{ill|Zōshūsai|de|Zōshūsai|ja|造酒司|zh|造酒司}}), consist of the O-miyaburushi deity associated with food and sake and two deities governing the water used in brewing. All four O-miyaburushi shrines were formal shrines, with their offerings entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}; in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859) the divine Rank of Sakaden Shrine appears to have been raised to Lower Fifth Rank, and in the 3rd year of Jōgan ({{ill|862nd year|de|862nd year|ja|862年|zh|862年}}) the deities Sakayamitodono Otoko-no-kami and Sakayamitodono Megami were elevated to Upper Fifth Rank. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=32}} ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Water (1 shrine) ::: This is the deity enshrined in the office of the {{ill|Shusui-shi|de|Shusui-shi|ja|主水司|zh|主水司}}, which oversees water and ice procurement—the deity being enshrined at {{ill|Narutai Shrine|de|Narutai Shrine|ja|鳴雷神社|zh|鳴雷神社}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=33}} ; Capital Deities (3 shrines: Taishikoto-no-mikoto, Hisashimitachinomiya, and Hayai Shrine) : These are the deities enshrined within the capital of Heian-kyo, as listed in the Kami Name Register. All three are formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭}} and the {{ill|Niinamesai|de|Niinamesai|ja|新嘗祭|zh|新嘗祭}}, and particularly the deities Taishikoto-no-mikoto and Hisashimitachinomiya were also honored at the {{ill|Sounamatsuri|de|Sounamatsuri|ja|相嘗祭|zh|相嘗祭}}. ; {{ill|Ame-no-Osoroshi-no-mikoto|de|Ame-no-Osoroshi-no-mikoto|ja|天児屋命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天児屋命|1=Ame-no-Koyane|lt=Taitatari-no-mikoto|lt_ja=太詔戸命神|lt_de=Taitatari-no-mikoto|lt_zh=Taitatari-no-mikoto}} :: In the Muromachi period, this deity of ritual recitations (prayers) was enshrined to the west. His divine Rank was raised to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859), later to Upper Third Rank. He is now defunct. In the Kami Name Register he appears as the formal shrine in Yamato Province—namely, the “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with Mori Shrine in {{ill|Nara Prefecture|de|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県|zh|奈良县}}/{{ill|Tenri City|de|Tenri City|ja|天理市|zh|天理市}}) and in Tsushima Province as “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with {{ill|Taishikoto Shrine|de|Taishikoto Shrine|ja|太祝詞神社|zh|太祝詞神社}} in {{ill|Nagasaki Prefecture|de|Nagasaki Prefecture|ja|長崎県|zh|长崎县}}/{{ill|Tsushima City|de|Tsushima City|ja|対馬市|zh|对马市}}); these are regarded as his original enclosures. ; {{ill|Kushimachinomiya|de|Kushimachinomiya|ja|櫛真智命|zh|櫛真智命|lt=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_ja=久慈真智命神|lt_de=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_zh=Hisashimitachinomiya}} :: Enshrined to the west of the Shijōbōmon area, this divinized deity of divination was elevated to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} (859) and is now defunct. According to the Kami Name Register, his original shrine is the “Tenkōzan Zari Kushinomiya Shrine” in Yamato Province (with candidate shrines in [[Kashihara City]] of Nara Prefecture, including Tenkōzan Shrine and Kuninotokotachi Shrine) and is considered his original. ; {{ill|Hayai Shrine|de|Hayai Shrine|ja|隼神社|zh|隼神社}} :: Enshrined within the Shujakuin of the Later Palace, this deity was raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the sixteenth year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan}} ({{ill|874th year|de|874th year|ja|874年|zh|874年}}) and is now maintained as an associated shrine of {{ill|Mangai Shrine|de|Mangai Shrine|ja|梛神社|zh|梛神社}} (located in {{ill|Nakagyo Ward|de|Nakagyo Ward|ja|中京区|zh|中京区}} of Kyoto City). For details, see the section "[[Mangai Shrine#Hayai Shrine]]". == == 式外社 == 『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが、同帳に記載の無い神社。 {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=2 | 文献 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=3 | 比定社 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" rowspan=2 | 集成 |- !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 神名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 記事 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 社名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 所在地 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 備考 |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|'''[[大内裏|宮中]]''' |- |'''庭火神'''

This is a '''List of Shikinaisha in the Imperial Palace'''. Or the list of shrines in [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which is present in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}. On this page we will also cover the {{ill|Shikigeisha|ja|式外社|1=Shikigeisha|12=draft}} of [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which are shrines that are known to have existed at that time due to other historical records, such as the [[Rikkokushi]], but for some reason were excluded from the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳|12=draft}}.
