式内社の位置}}]] [[File:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|[[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] 配置図}}]] In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the Kami Name Register begins by listing 36 shrines in the palace and 3 in the capital. As the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] was compiled in the mid-[[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]], “in the palace” and “in the capital” refer respectively to those within the Heian Palace ([[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian Capital]]/[[:en:Heian Palace|Imperial Palace]]) and to those within the city of Heian-kyo. The following explains each enshrined deity. ; Palace Deities (30 major shrines, 6 minor shrines) : This term refers to the deities enshrined within the Imperial Palace of [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian Capital]], as reported by {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=8}}. The rituals for the 8 Imperial Miko deities were handed down at one of the [[:en:Three Palace Sanctuaries|Three Palace Sanctuaries]] (Shinden), and it is presumed that the worship of the other palace deities was likewise inherited within the “Tenjin-Chigi” section of the Shinden. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}} :; Deities Enshrined in the Western Wing of the [[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] (21 shrines) ::: These are the deities enshrined at the [[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]], one of the {{ill|Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|de|Zwei Ämter und Acht Ministerien|ja|二官八省|zh|二官八省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|qq=}}. The Jingi-kan comprised an Eastern and a Western Wing (Saien); while the Eastern Wing performed administrative duties, the Western Wing handled ritual functions. The deities in the Western Wing, sometimes termed the “Emperor’s Shinto Altar” {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176}}, occupy a key position, although the ancestral deity [[:en:Amaterasu|amaterasu]] is not enshrined there. These gods were served by shrine maidens known as [[:en:Miko|Miko]], called “Mikanna.” For each served deity there were 2 chief Mikos (later 3), 1 Zasama Miko, 1 Mikado Miko, and 1 Ikushima Miko. All 21 enshrined deities were designated formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]. ::: Although the Jingi-kan declined and fell into ruin during the medieval period, its continuation is attested until the [[Ōnin]] period (from [[:en:1467|1467年]] to [[:en:1468|1468年]]), but by the [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei Period]] (from [[:en:1469|1469年]] to [[:en:1486|1486年]]) it appears to have been completely abolished. In the [[:en:Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tenshō Period]] 18th year ([[:en:1590|1590年]]), eight Shinden were enshrined within the precincts of [[:en:Yoshida Shrine|Yoshida Shrine]], and in the [[:en:Keichō|Keichō Period]] 14th year ([[:en:1609|1609年]]) Yoshida Shrine was designated as the substitute for the Jingi-kan. After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], a Shinden enshrining the Eight Gods and Tenjin-Chigi was built within the Imperial Palace, and the ritual practice was maintained; however, since ancient rites had become entirely extinct, the current ceremonies are completely different. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176-201}} :::; {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|lt=Mikamisai-shin|lt_ja=御巫祭神|lt_de=Mikamisai-shin|lt_zh=Mikamisai-shin|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}} (8 shrines: {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiharunohime|qq=}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaomiharunohime|qq=}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsumiharunohime|qq=}}, {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Namiharunohime|qq=}}, {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashiharunohime|qq=}}, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=}}, {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=}}, and {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}). ::::: These 8 deities were served by the chief Miko ({{ill|Oomikanna|de|Oomikanna|ja|大御巫|zh|大御巫|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oomikanna|qq=}}). According to the personnel regulations set out in the {{ill|Reishūkai|de|Reishūkai|ja|令集解|zh|令集解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reishūkai|qq=}}, in the Nara period the chief Miko system consisted of 2 “Wakoku Miko,” but by the Heian period, as recorded in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], it had expanded to 3—for the Emperor, the {{ill|Empress|de|Kaiserin|ja|中宮|zh|中宫|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|qq=}}, and the [[:en:Crown prince|Crown Prince]]. These 8 deities, which include 5 governing souls, one mediating between ruler and subjects ({{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=}}), one governing food ({{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=}}), and one governing language ({{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}), thus serve to pacify the spirit, were enshrined in the {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}}. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} ([[:en:859|859年]]), {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiharunohime|qq=}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaomiharunohime|qq=}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsumiharunohime|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashiharunohime|qq=}} were promoted to First Rank, while {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Namiharunohime|qq=}} was raised to Second Rank. Among these, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=}} is said to have passed down a small shrine in the Shuze area of Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, [[:en:Yoshida Shrine|Yoshida Shrine]], is also well known. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=184-187}} :::; {{ill|Zasama-no-kami|de|Zasama-no-kami|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|lt=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_ja=座摩巫祭神|lt_de=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_zh=Zasama-mikanna-shin|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama-no-kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikasuri no Kami|qq=}} (5 shrines: {{ill|Ikuni-no-kami|de|Ikuni-no-kami|ja|生井神|zh|生井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikuni-no-kami|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukunaga Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunanagai-no-kami|qq=}}, {{ill|Hapihi-no-kami|de|Hapihi-no-kami|ja|波比祇神|zh|波比祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hapihi-no-kami|qq=}}, and {{ill|Asuha-no-kami|de|Asuha-no-kami|ja|阿須波神|zh|阿须波神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asuha-no-kami|qq=}}). ::::: These 5 deities were served by a Zasama Miko, who—unlike the other Mikos—was stipulated in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] to be the daughter of the {{ill|Tokagenokuzō|de|Tokagenokuzō|ja|闘鶏国造|1=Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|2=ja|3=闘鶏国造|zh|闘鶏国造|1=Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|2=ja|3=闘鶏国造|lt=Tokagenokuzō|lt_ja=都下国造|lt_de=Tokagenokuzō|lt_zh=Tokagenokuzō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokagenokuzō|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. They comprise three deities safeguarding water and two safeguarding the premises, collectively regarded as deities protecting the palace. Their divine Ranks were elevated to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859). Among these, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukunaga Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunanagai-no-kami|qq=}} are said to have transmitted a small shrine in Fukunaga-cho, Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama Shrine|qq=}}, is known in Osaka. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Zasama-shin|de|Zasama-shin|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama-shin|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikasuri no Kami|qq=}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=187-188}} :::; {{ill|Mikado-no-kami|de|Mikado-no-kami|ja|御門巫祭神|zh|御門巫祭神|lt=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_ja=櫛石窓神|lt_de=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_zh=櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikado-no-kami|qq=}} (8 shrines: 4 for the {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|qq=}} and 4 for the {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|qq=}}) ::::: These 8 deities were served by the Mikado Miko. They enshrined the four gates of the outer perimeter of the {{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|内裏|zh|内裏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Palace|qq=}}—namely, the East Gate ({{ill|Kenchunmon|de|Kenchunmon|ja|建春門|zh|建春门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenchunmon|qq=}}), South Gate ({{ill|Kenreimon|de|Kenreimon|ja|建礼門|zh|建礼门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenreimon|qq=}}), West Gate ({{ill|Gikyuimon|de|Gikyuimon|ja|宜秋門|zh|宜秋门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gikyuimon|qq=}}), and North Gate ({{ill|Sakuhimon|de|Sakuhimon|ja|朔平門|zh|朔平门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakuhimon|qq=}}). One shrine each for {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|qq=}} and {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|qq=}} was enshrined, although the usual festival was held at the Western Wing of the Jingi-kan. There is a theory that because the deities named “Kushiishi Mado-no-kami” and “Toyoshi Mado-no-kami” were enshrined as natural stones—similar to the four guardian deities enshrined as natural stones in the precincts of [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Shrine]]—they were in fact enshrined as natural stones at each gate. Their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859). An associated shrine, {{ill|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|de|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|ja|櫛石窓神社|zh|櫛石窓神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado Shrine|qq=}}, located in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] in [[:en:Tamba-Sasayama|Tamba Sasayama]], is regarded as the original. :::; {{ill|Ikushima-no-kami|de|Ikushima-no-kami|ja|生島神|zh|生島神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikushima-no-kami|qq=}} and {{ill|Ashishima-no-kami|de|Ashishima-no-kami|ja|足島神|zh|足島神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashishima-no-kami|qq=}} (2 shrines) ::::: These 2 deities were served by the Ikushima Miko. According to the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kogo Shūi]], they are regarded as the spirits of the nation (the “Great Eight Islands”) and serve as a divine underpinning for the Emperor’s rule. Their divine Ranks were raised to Lower Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859). Associated shrines include [[:en:Ikukunitama Shrine|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine]] (Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture) and [[:en:Ikushimatarushima Shrine|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine]] (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture). {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=189-192}} ::: The deities enshrined in the Jingi-kan are described as radiating outward in concentric circles—from the Emperor’s body (served by the Imperial Miko), to the palace (served by the Zasama Miko), to the outer gates (served by the Mikado Miko), and finally to the land (served by the Ikushima Miko). In particular, because associated shrines such as {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama Shrine|qq=}} and [[:en:Ikukunitama Shrine|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine]] remain in Naniwa, it is theorized that the rites once performed at Naniwa Palace continued into the Heian period, with the existence of the {{ill|Ya-shima Festival|de|Ya-shima Festival|ja|八十島祭|zh|八十岛祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ya-shima Festival|qq=}} during imperial enthronements emphasizing Naniwa’s importance. {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=190-192}} ; Deities of the Imperial Household Ministry (3 shrines: Son Shrine and two Kan Shrines) ::: These refer to the deities enshrined within the [[:en:Ministry of the Imperial Household|Imperial Household Ministry]], whose exact identities vary – some sources state that the Son deity protects the garden pond, others that the Kan deity wards off epidemics – but in any case they have been enshrined since before the Heian period. All are formal shrines, and their offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]; their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Third Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859). For further details, see the article on {{ill|Sonkan Shrine|de|Sonkan Shrine|ja|園韓神社|zh|园韩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonkan Shrine|qq=}}. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Court Meals (3 shrines: Mishokutsunushi Shrine, Hurai Shrine, and Koubai Shrine) ::: These deities, under the auspices of the ministry responsible for court meals (the {{ill|Daizen-shoku|de|Daizen-shoku|ja|大膳職|zh|大膳职|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daizen-shoku|qq=}}), include {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=}}, who governs food; {{ill|Hurai Shrine|de|Hurai Shrine|ja|火雷神社|zh|火雷神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hurai Shrine|qq=}}, who governs water; and {{ill|Koubai Shrine|de|Koubai Shrine|ja|高倍神社|zh|高倍神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koubai Shrine|qq=}}, associated with earthenware. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859), the divine Rank of {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=}} was raised to Lower Third Rank, that of Hurai Shrine to Upper Fifth Rank, and that of Koubai Shrine to Lower Fifth Rank. According to the anecdotal record [[:en:Takahashi Ujibumi|Takahashi Shibun]], see also [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection – Awa Zashinja (Awa Province, Awa District)] and [{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 'Gunsho Ruijū Fifth Volume'] in the National Diet Library Digital Collection, additional details are provided. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Sake Production (4 shrines at O-miyaburushi Shrine; 2 shrines at Sakaden Shrine) ::: These deities, affiliated with the ministry responsible for sake brewing (the {{ill|Zōshūsai|de|Zōshūsai|ja|造酒司|zh|造酒司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zōshūsai|qq=}}), consist of the O-miyaburushi deity associated with food and sake and two deities governing the water used in brewing. All four O-miyaburushi shrines were formal shrines, with their offerings entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]; in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859) the divine Rank of Sakaden Shrine appears to have been raised to Lower Fifth Rank, and in the 3rd year of Jōgan ([[:en:862|862年]]) the deities Sakayamitodono Otoko-no-kami and Sakayamitodono Megami were elevated to Upper Fifth Rank. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=32}} ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Water (1 shrine) ::: This is the deity enshrined in the office of the {{ill|Shusui-shi|de|Shusui-shi|ja|主水司|zh|主水司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shusui-shi|qq=}}, which oversees water and ice procurement—the deity being enshrined at {{ill|Narutai Shrine|de|Narutai Shrine|ja|鳴雷神社|zh|鳴雷神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Narutai Shrine|qq=}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=33}} ; Capital Deities (3 shrines: Taishikoto-no-mikoto, Hisashimitachinomiya, and Hayai Shrine) : These are the deities enshrined within the capital of Heian-kyo, as listed in the Kami Name Register. All three are formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]], and particularly the deities Taishikoto-no-mikoto and Hisashimitachinomiya were also honored at the {{ill|Sounamatsuri|de|Sounamatsuri|ja|相嘗祭|zh|相嘗祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sounamatsuri|qq=}}. ; [[:en:Ame-no-Koyane|Taitatari-no-mikoto]] :: In the Muromachi period, this deity of ritual recitations (prayers) was enshrined to the west. His divine Rank was raised to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859), later to Upper Third Rank. He is now defunct. In the Kami Name Register he appears as the formal shrine in Yamato Province—namely, the “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with Mori Shrine in [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]/[[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri City]]) and in Tsushima Province as “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with {{ill|Taishikoto Shrine|de|Taishikoto Shrine|ja|太祝詞神社|zh|太祝詞神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishikoto Shrine|qq=}} in [[:en:Nagasaki Prefecture|Nagasaki Prefecture]]/[[:en:Tsushima, Nagasaki|Tsushima City]]); these are regarded as his original enclosures. ; {{ill|Kushimachinomiya|de|Kushimachinomiya|ja|櫛真智命|zh|櫛真智命|lt=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_ja=久慈真智命神|lt_de=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_zh=Hisashimitachinomiya|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushimachinomiya|qq=}} :: Enshrined to the west of the Shijōbōmon area, this divinized deity of divination was elevated to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} (859) and is now defunct. According to the Kami Name Register, his original shrine is the “Tenkōzan Zari Kushinomiya Shrine” in Yamato Province (with candidate shrines in [[Kashihara City]] of Nara Prefecture, including Tenkōzan Shrine and Kuninotokotachi Shrine) and is considered his original. ; {{ill|Hayai Shrine|de|Hayai Shrine|ja|隼神社|zh|隼神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayai Shrine|qq=}} :: Enshrined within the Shujakuin of the Later Palace, this deity was raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the sixteenth year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=}} ([[:en:874|874年]]) and is now maintained as an associated shrine of {{ill|Mangai Shrine|de|Mangai Shrine|ja|梛神社|zh|梛神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mangai Shrine|qq=}} (located in [[:en:Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto|Nakagyo Ward]] of Kyoto City). For details, see the section "[[Mangai Shrine#Hayai Shrine]]". == == 式外社 == 『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが、同帳に記載の無い神社。 {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=2 | 文献 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=3 | 比定社 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" rowspan=2 | 集成 |- !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 神名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 記事 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 社名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 所在地 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 備考 |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|'''[[大内裏|宮中]]''' |- |'''庭火神'''

This is a '''List of Shikinaisha in the Imperial Palace'''. Or the list of shrines in [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which is present in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. On this page we will also cover the {{ill|Shikigeisha|ja|式外社|1=Shikigeisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigeisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigeisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which are shrines that are known to have existed at that time due to other historical records, such as the [[Rikkokushi]], but for some reason were excluded from the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. 式内社の位置}}]] [[File:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|[[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] 配置図}}]] In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the Kami Name Register begins by listing 36 shrines in the palace and 3 in the capital. As the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] was compiled in the mid-[[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]], “in the palace” and “in the capital” refer respectively to those within the Heian Palace ([[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian Capital]]/[[:en:Heian Palace|Imperial Palace]]) and to those within the city of Heian-kyo. The following explains each enshrined deity. ; Palace Deities (30 major shrines, 6 minor shrines) : This term refers to the deities enshrined within the Imperial Palace of [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian Capital]], as reported by {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=8}}. The rituals for the 8 Imperial Miko deities were handed down at one of the [[:en:Three Palace Sanctuaries|Three Palace Sanctuaries]] (Shinden), and it is presumed that the worship of the other palace deities was likewise inherited within the “Tenjin-Chigi” section of the Shinden. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}} :; Deities Enshrined in the Western Wing of the [[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] (21 shrines) ::: These are the deities enshrined at the [[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]], one of the {{ill|Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|de|Zwei Ämter und Acht Ministerien|ja|二官八省|zh|二官八省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日本の官制}}. The Jingi-kan comprised an Eastern and a Western Wing (Saien); while the Eastern Wing performed administrative duties, the Western Wing handled ritual functions. The deities in the Western Wing, sometimes termed the “Emperor’s Shinto Altar” {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176}}, occupy a key position, although the ancestral deity [[:en:Amaterasu|amaterasu]] is not enshrined there. These gods were served by shrine maidens known as [[:en:Miko|Miko]], called “Mikanna.” For each served deity there were 2 chief Mikos (later 3), 1 Zasama Miko, 1 Mikado Miko, and 1 Ikushima Miko. All 21 enshrined deities were designated formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]. ::: Although the Jingi-kan declined and fell into ruin during the medieval period, its continuation is attested until the [[Ōnin]] period (from [[:en:1467|1467年]] to [[:en:1468|1468年]]), but by the [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei Period]] (from [[:en:1469|1469年]] to [[:en:1486|1486年]]) it appears to have been completely abolished. In the [[:en:Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tenshō Period]] 18th year ([[:en:1590|1590年]]), eight Shinden were enshrined within the precincts of [[:en:Yoshida Shrine|Yoshida Shrine]], and in the [[:en:Keichō|Keichō Period]] 14th year ([[:en:1609|1609年]]) Yoshida Shrine was designated as the substitute for the Jingi-kan. After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], a Shinden enshrining the Eight Gods and Tenjin-Chigi was built within the Imperial Palace, and the ritual practice was maintained; however, since ancient rites had become entirely extinct, the current ceremonies are completely different. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176-201}} :::; {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|lt=Mikamisai-shin|lt_ja=御巫祭神|lt_de=Mikamisai-shin|lt_zh=Mikamisai-shin|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}} (8 shrines: {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カミムスビ}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaomiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タカミムスビ}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsumiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Namiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天活玉命}}, {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}}, {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}, and {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}). ::::: These 8 deities were served by the chief Miko ({{ill|Oomikanna|de|Oomikanna|ja|大御巫|zh|大御巫|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oomikanna|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). According to the personnel regulations set out in the {{ill|Reishūkai|de|Reishūkai|ja|令集解|zh|令集解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reishūkai|qq=}}, in the Nara period the chief Miko system consisted of 2 “Wakoku Miko,” but by the Heian period, as recorded in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], it had expanded to 3—for the Emperor, the {{ill|Empress|de|Kaiserin|ja|中宮|zh|中宫|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|qq=}}, and the [[:en:Crown prince|Crown Prince]]. These 8 deities, which include 5 governing souls, one mediating between ruler and subjects ({{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}}), one governing food ({{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}), and one governing language ({{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}), thus serve to pacify the spirit, were enshrined in the {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}}. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ([[:en:859|859年]]), {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カミムスビ}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaomiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タカミムスビ}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsumiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} were promoted to First Rank, while {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Namiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天活玉命}} was raised to Second Rank. Among these, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} is said to have passed down a small shrine in the Shuze area of Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, [[:en:Yoshida Shrine|Yoshida Shrine]], is also well known. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=184-187}} :::; {{ill|Zasama-no-kami|de|Zasama-no-kami|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|lt=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_ja=座摩巫祭神|lt_de=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_zh=Zasama-mikanna-shin|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama-no-kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikasuri no Kami|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (5 shrines: {{ill|Ikuni-no-kami|de|Ikuni-no-kami|ja|生井神|zh|生井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikuni-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukunaga Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunanagai-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}, {{ill|Hapihi-no-kami|de|Hapihi-no-kami|ja|波比祇神|zh|波比祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hapihi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}, and {{ill|Asuha-no-kami|de|Asuha-no-kami|ja|阿須波神|zh|阿须波神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asuha-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}). ::::: These 5 deities were served by a Zasama Miko, who—unlike the other Mikos—was stipulated in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] to be the daughter of the {{ill|Tokagenokuzō|de|Tokagenokuzō|ja|闘鶏国造|1=Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|2=ja|3=闘鶏国造|zh|闘鶏国造|1=Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|2=ja|3=闘鶏国造|lt=Tokagenokuzō|lt_ja=都下国造|lt_de=Tokagenokuzō|lt_zh=Tokagenokuzō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokagenokuzō|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. They comprise three deities safeguarding water and two safeguarding the premises, collectively regarded as deities protecting the palace. Their divine Ranks were elevated to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). Among these, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukunaga Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunanagai-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}} are said to have transmitted a small shrine in Fukunaga-cho, Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 坐摩神社}}, is known in Osaka. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Zasama-shin|de|Zasama-shin|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama-shin|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikasuri no Kami|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=187-188}} :::; {{ill|Mikado-no-kami|de|Mikado-no-kami|ja|御門巫祭神|zh|御門巫祭神|lt=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_ja=櫛石窓神|lt_de=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_zh=櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8 shrines: 4 for the {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}} and 4 for the {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}}) ::::: These 8 deities were served by the Mikado Miko. They enshrined the four gates of the outer perimeter of the {{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|内裏|zh|内裏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Palace|qq=}}—namely, the East Gate ({{ill|Kenchunmon|de|Kenchunmon|ja|建春門|zh|建春门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenchunmon|qq=}}), South Gate ({{ill|Kenreimon|de|Kenreimon|ja|建礼門|zh|建礼门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenreimon|qq=}}), West Gate ({{ill|Gikyuimon|de|Gikyuimon|ja|宜秋門|zh|宜秋门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gikyuimon|qq=}}), and North Gate ({{ill|Sakuhimon|de|Sakuhimon|ja|朔平門|zh|朔平门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakuhimon|qq=}}). One shrine each for {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}} and {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}} was enshrined, although the usual festival was held at the Western Wing of the Jingi-kan. There is a theory that because the deities named “Kushiishi Mado-no-kami” and “Toyoshi Mado-no-kami” were enshrined as natural stones—similar to the four guardian deities enshrined as natural stones in the precincts of [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Shrine]]—they were in fact enshrined as natural stones at each gate. Their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). An associated shrine, {{ill|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|de|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|ja|櫛石窓神社|zh|櫛石窓神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado Shrine|qq=}}, located in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] in [[:en:Tamba-Sasayama|Tamba Sasayama]], is regarded as the original. :::; {{ill|Ikushima-no-kami|de|Ikushima-no-kami|ja|生島神|zh|生島神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikushima-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ashishima-no-kami|de|Ashishima-no-kami|ja|足島神|zh|足島神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashishima-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2 shrines) ::::: These 2 deities were served by the Ikushima Miko. According to the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kogo Shūi]], they are regarded as the spirits of the nation (the “Great Eight Islands”) and serve as a divine underpinning for the Emperor’s rule. Their divine Ranks were raised to Lower Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). Associated shrines include [[:en:Ikukunitama Shrine|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine]] (Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture) and [[:en:Ikushimatarushima Shrine|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine]] (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture). {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=189-192}} ::: The deities enshrined in the Jingi-kan are described as radiating outward in concentric circles—from the Emperor’s body (served by the Imperial Miko), to the palace (served by the Zasama Miko), to the outer gates (served by the Mikado Miko), and finally to the land (served by the Ikushima Miko). In particular, because associated shrines such as {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 坐摩神社}} and [[:en:Ikukunitama Shrine|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine]] remain in Naniwa, it is theorized that the rites once performed at Naniwa Palace continued into the Heian period, with the existence of the {{ill|Ya-shima Festival|de|Ya-shima Festival|ja|八十島祭|zh|八十岛祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ya-shima Festival|qq=}} during imperial enthronements emphasizing Naniwa’s importance. {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=190-192}} ; Deities of the Imperial Household Ministry (3 shrines: Son Shrine and two Kan Shrines) ::: These refer to the deities enshrined within the [[:en:Ministry of the Imperial Household|Imperial Household Ministry]], whose exact identities vary – some sources state that the Son deity protects the garden pond, others that the Kan deity wards off epidemics – but in any case they have been enshrined since before the Heian period. All are formal shrines, and their offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]; their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Third Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). For further details, see the article on {{ill|Sonkan Shrine|de|Sonkan Shrine|ja|園韓神社|zh|园韩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonkan Shrine|qq=}}. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Court Meals (3 shrines: Mishokutsunushi Shrine, Hurai Shrine, and Koubai Shrine) ::: These deities, under the auspices of the ministry responsible for court meals (the {{ill|Daizen-shoku|de|Daizen-shoku|ja|大膳職|zh|大膳职|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daizen-shoku|qq=}}), include {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}, who governs food; {{ill|Hurai Shrine|de|Hurai Shrine|ja|火雷神社|zh|火雷神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hurai Shrine|qq=}}, who governs water; and {{ill|Koubai Shrine|de|Koubai Shrine|ja|高倍神社|zh|高倍神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koubai Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with earthenware. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859), the divine Rank of {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}} was raised to Lower Third Rank, that of Hurai Shrine to Upper Fifth Rank, and that of Koubai Shrine to Lower Fifth Rank. According to the anecdotal record [[:en:Takahashi Ujibumi|Takahashi Shibun]], see also [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection – Awa Zashinja (Awa Province, Awa District)] and [{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 'Gunsho Ruijū Fifth Volume'] in the National Diet Library Digital Collection, additional details are provided. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Sake Production (4 shrines at O-miyaburushi Shrine; 2 shrines at Sakaden Shrine) ::: These deities, affiliated with the ministry responsible for sake brewing (the {{ill|Zōshūsai|de|Zōshūsai|ja|造酒司|zh|造酒司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zōshūsai|qq=}}), consist of the O-miyaburushi deity associated with food and sake and two deities governing the water used in brewing. All four O-miyaburushi shrines were formal shrines, with their offerings entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]; in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859) the divine Rank of Sakaden Shrine appears to have been raised to Lower Fifth Rank, and in the 3rd year of Jōgan ([[:en:862|862年]]) the deities Sakayamitodono Otoko-no-kami and Sakayamitodono Megami were elevated to Upper Fifth Rank. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=32}} ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Water (1 shrine) ::: This is the deity enshrined in the office of the {{ill|Shusui-shi|de|Shusui-shi|ja|主水司|zh|主水司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shusui-shi|qq=}}, which oversees water and ice procurement—the deity being enshrined at {{ill|Narutai Shrine|de|Narutai Shrine|ja|鳴雷神社|zh|鳴雷神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Narutai Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=33}} ; Capital Deities (3 shrines: Taishikoto-no-mikoto, Hisashimitachinomiya, and Hayai Shrine) : These are the deities enshrined within the capital of Heian-kyo, as listed in the Kami Name Register. All three are formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]], and particularly the deities Taishikoto-no-mikoto and Hisashimitachinomiya were also honored at the {{ill|Sounamatsuri|de|Sounamatsuri|ja|相嘗祭|zh|相嘗祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sounamatsuri|qq=}}. ; [[:en:Ame-no-Koyane|Taitatari-no-mikoto]] :: In the Muromachi period, this deity of ritual recitations (prayers) was enshrined to the west. His divine Rank was raised to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859), later to Upper Third Rank. He is now defunct. In the Kami Name Register he appears as the formal shrine in Yamato Province—namely, the “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with Mori Shrine in [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]/[[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri City]]) and in Tsushima Province as “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with {{ill|Taishikoto Shrine|de|Taishikoto Shrine|ja|太祝詞神社|zh|太祝詞神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishikoto Shrine|qq=}} in [[:en:Nagasaki Prefecture|Nagasaki Prefecture]]/[[:en:Tsushima, Nagasaki|Tsushima City]]); these are regarded as his original enclosures. ; {{ill|Kushimachinomiya|de|Kushimachinomiya|ja|櫛真智命|zh|櫛真智命|lt=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_ja=久慈真智命神|lt_de=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_zh=Hisashimitachinomiya|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushimachinomiya|qq=}} :: Enshrined to the west of the Shijōbōmon area, this divinized deity of divination was elevated to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859) and is now defunct. According to the Kami Name Register, his original shrine is the “Tenkōzan Zari Kushinomiya Shrine” in Yamato Province (with candidate shrines in [[Kashihara City]] of Nara Prefecture, including Tenkōzan Shrine and Kuninotokotachi Shrine) and is considered his original. ; {{ill|Hayai Shrine|de|Hayai Shrine|ja|隼神社|zh|隼神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayai Shrine|qq=}} :: Enshrined within the Shujakuin of the Later Palace, this deity was raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the sixteenth year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ([[:en:874|874年]]) and is now maintained as an associated shrine of {{ill|Mangai Shrine|de|Mangai Shrine|ja|梛神社|zh|梛神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mangai Shrine|qq=}} (located in [[:en:Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto|Nakagyo Ward]] of Kyoto City). This is a '''List of Shikinaisha in the Imperial Palace'''. Or the list of shrines in [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which is present in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. On this page we will also cover the {{ill|Shikigeisha|ja|式外社|1=Shikigeisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigeisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigeisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which are shrines that are known to have existed at that time due to other historical records, such as the [[Rikkokushi]], but for some reason were excluded from the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. 式内社の位置}}]] [[File:平安京 神祇官配置図.png|thumb|200px|right|{{center|[[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] 配置図}}]] In the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], the Kami Name Register begins by listing 36 shrines in the palace and 3 in the capital. As the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] was compiled in the mid-[[:en:Heian period|Heian Period]], “in the palace” and “in the capital” refer respectively to those within the Heian Palace ([[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian Capital]]/[[:en:Heian Palace|Imperial Palace]]) and to those within the city of Heian-kyo. The following explains each enshrined deity. ; Palace Deities (30 major shrines, 6 minor shrines) : This term refers to the deities enshrined within the Imperial Palace of [[:en:Heian-kyō|Heian Capital]], as reported by {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=8}}. The rituals for the 8 Imperial Miko deities were handed down at one of the [[:en:Three Palace Sanctuaries|Three Palace Sanctuaries]] (Shinden), and it is presumed that the worship of the other palace deities was likewise inherited within the “Tenjin-Chigi” section of the Shinden. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}} :; Deities Enshrined in the Western Wing of the [[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] (21 shrines) ::: These are the deities enshrined at the [[:en:Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]], one of the {{ill|Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|de|Zwei Ämter und Acht Ministerien|ja|二官八省|zh|二官八省|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Two Bureaus and Eight Ministries|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日本の官制}}. The Jingi-kan comprised an Eastern and a Western Wing (Saien); while the Eastern Wing performed administrative duties, the Western Wing handled ritual functions. The deities in the Western Wing, sometimes termed the “Emperor’s Shinto Altar” {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176}}, occupy a key position, although the ancestral deity [[:en:Amaterasu|amaterasu]] is not enshrined there. These gods were served by shrine maidens known as [[:en:Miko|Miko]], called “Mikanna.” For each served deity there were 2 chief Mikos (later 3), 1 Zasama Miko, 1 Mikado Miko, and 1 Ikushima Miko. All 21 enshrined deities were designated formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]. ::: Although the Jingi-kan declined and fell into ruin during the medieval period, its continuation is attested until the [[:en:Ōnin|Ōnin]] period (from [[:en:1467|1467年]] to [[:en:1468|1468年]]), but by the [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei Period]] (from [[:en:1469|1469年]] to [[:en:1486|1486年]]) it appears to have been completely abolished. In the [[:en:Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Tenshō Period]] 18th year ([[:en:1590|1590年]]), eight Shinden were enshrined within the precincts of [[:en:Yoshida Shrine|Yoshida Shrine]], and in the [[:en:Keichō|Keichō Period]] 14th year ([[:en:1609|1609年]]) Yoshida Shrine was designated as the substitute for the Jingi-kan. After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], a Shinden enshrining the Eight Gods and Tenjin-Chigi was built within the Imperial Palace, and the ritual practice was maintained; however, since ancient rites had become entirely extinct, the current ceremonies are completely different. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=3-11}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=176-201}} :::; {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|lt=Mikamisai-shin|lt_ja=御巫祭神|lt_de=Mikamisai-shin|lt_zh=Mikamisai-shin|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}} (8 shrines: {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カミムスビ}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaomiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タカミムスビ}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsumiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Namiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天活玉命}}, {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}}, {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}, and {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}). ::::: These 8 deities were served by the chief Miko ({{ill|Oomikanna|de|Oomikanna|ja|大御巫|zh|大御巫|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oomikanna|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). According to the personnel regulations set out in the {{ill|Reishūkai|de|Reishūkai|ja|令集解|zh|令集解|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reishūkai|qq=}}, in the Nara period the chief Miko system consisted of 2 “Wakoku Miko,” but by the Heian period, as recorded in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]], it had expanded to 3—for the Emperor, the {{ill|Empress|de|Kaiserin|ja|中宮|zh|中宫|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|qq=}}, and the [[:en:Crown prince|Crown Prince]]. These 8 deities, which include 5 governing souls, one mediating between ruler and subjects ({{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}}), one governing food ({{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}), and one governing language ({{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|de|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主神|zh|事代主神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}), thus serve to pacify the spirit, were enshrined in the {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}}. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ([[:en:859|859年]]), {{ill|Kamiharunohime|de|Kamiharunohime|ja|神産日神|zh|神産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カミムスビ}}, {{ill|Takaomiharunohime|de|Takaomiharunohime|ja|高御産日神|zh|高御産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaomiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to タカミムスビ}}, {{ill|Tamatsumiharunohime|de|Tamatsumiharunohime|ja|玉積産日神|zh|玉積産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsumiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and {{ill|Ashiharunohime|de|Ashiharunohime|ja|足産日神|zh|足産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} were promoted to First Rank, while {{ill|Namiharunohime|de|Namiharunohime|ja|生産日神|zh|生産日神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Namiharunohime|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天活玉命}} was raised to Second Rank. Among these, {{ill|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|de|O-miyaburushi-no-kami|ja|大宮売神|zh|大宮売神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/O-miyaburushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to オオミヤノメ}} is said to have passed down a small shrine in the Shuze area of Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, [[:en:Yoshida Shrine|Yoshida Shrine]], is also well known. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Hachishinden|de|Hachishinden|ja|八神殿|zh|Hachishinden|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachishinden|qq=}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=13-23}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=184-187}} :::; {{ill|Zasama-no-kami|de|Zasama-no-kami|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|lt=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_ja=座摩巫祭神|lt_de=Zasama-mikanna-shin|lt_zh=Zasama-mikanna-shin|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama-no-kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikasuri no Kami|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (5 shrines: {{ill|Ikuni-no-kami|de|Ikuni-no-kami|ja|生井神|zh|生井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikuni-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukunaga Shrine|qq=}}, {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunanagai-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}, {{ill|Hapihi-no-kami|de|Hapihi-no-kami|ja|波比祇神|zh|波比祇神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hapihi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}, and {{ill|Asuha-no-kami|de|Asuha-no-kami|ja|阿須波神|zh|阿须波神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asuha-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}}). ::::: These 5 deities were served by a Zasama Miko, who—unlike the other Mikos—was stipulated in the [[:en:Engishiki|Engishiki]] to be the daughter of the {{ill|Tokagenokuzō|de|Tokagenokuzō|ja|闘鶏国造|1=Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|2=ja|3=闘鶏国造|zh|闘鶏国造|1=Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|2=ja|3=闘鶏国造|lt=Tokagenokuzō|lt_ja=都下国造|lt_de=Tokagenokuzō|lt_zh=Tokagenokuzō|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokagenokuzō|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuge no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}}. They comprise three deities safeguarding water and two safeguarding the premises, collectively regarded as deities protecting the palace. Their divine Ranks were elevated to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). Among these, {{ill|Fukunaga Shrine|de|Fukunaga Shrine|ja|福長神社|zh|福长神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukunaga Shrine|qq=}} and {{ill|Tsunanagai-no-kami|de|Tsunanagai-no-kami|ja|綱長井神|zh|綱長井神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsunanagai-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 座摩神}} are said to have transmitted a small shrine in Fukunaga-cho, Kamigyo Ward, Kyoto City; an associated shrine, {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 坐摩神社}}, is known in Osaka. For further details, see the article on {{ill|Zasama-shin|de|Zasama-shin|ja|座摩神|1=Ikasuri no Kami|2=ja|3=座摩神|4=zh|5=坐摩巫祭神|zh|座摩神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama-shin|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikasuri no Kami|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=24-25}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=187-188}} :::; {{ill|Mikado-no-kami|de|Mikado-no-kami|ja|御門巫祭神|zh|御門巫祭神|lt=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_ja=櫛石窓神|lt_de=Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|lt_zh=櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (8 shrines: 4 for the {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}} and 4 for the {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}}) ::::: These 8 deities were served by the Mikado Miko. They enshrined the four gates of the outer perimeter of the {{ill|Imperial Palace|de|Kaiserpalast|ja|内裏|zh|内裏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial Palace|qq=}}—namely, the East Gate ({{ill|Kenchunmon|de|Kenchunmon|ja|建春門|zh|建春门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenchunmon|qq=}}), South Gate ({{ill|Kenreimon|de|Kenreimon|ja|建礼門|zh|建礼门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenreimon|qq=}}), West Gate ({{ill|Gikyuimon|de|Gikyuimon|ja|宜秋門|zh|宜秋门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gikyuimon|qq=}}), and North Gate ({{ill|Sakuhimon|de|Sakuhimon|ja|朔平門|zh|朔平门|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakuhimon|qq=}}). One shrine each for {{ill|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|de|Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|ja|櫛石窓神|zh|櫛石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}} and {{ill|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|de|Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|ja|豊石窓神|zh|豊石窓神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoshi Mado-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天石門別神}} was enshrined, although the usual festival was held at the Western Wing of the Jingi-kan. There is a theory that because the deities named “Kushiishi Mado-no-kami” and “Toyoshi Mado-no-kami” were enshrined as natural stones—similar to the four guardian deities enshrined as natural stones in the precincts of [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Shrine]]—they were in fact enshrined as natural stones at each gate. Their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). An associated shrine, {{ill|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|de|Kushiishi Mado Shrine|ja|櫛石窓神社|zh|櫛石窓神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiishi Mado Shrine|qq=}}, located in [[:en:Hyōgo Prefecture|Hyōgo Prefecture]] in [[:en:Tamba-Sasayama|Tamba Sasayama]], is regarded as the original. :::; {{ill|Ikushima-no-kami|de|Ikushima-no-kami|ja|生島神|zh|生島神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ikushima-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ashishima-no-kami|de|Ashishima-no-kami|ja|足島神|zh|足島神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ashishima-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (2 shrines) ::::: These 2 deities were served by the Ikushima Miko. According to the [[:en:Kogo Shūi|Kogo Shūi]], they are regarded as the spirits of the nation (the “Great Eight Islands”) and serve as a divine underpinning for the Emperor’s rule. Their divine Ranks were raised to Lower Fourth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). Associated shrines include [[:en:Ikukunitama Shrine|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine]] (Osaka City, Osaka Prefecture) and [[:en:Ikushimatarushima Shrine|Ikushima Ashishima Shrine]] (Ueda City, Nagano Prefecture). {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|pp=28-29}}{{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=189-192}} ::: The deities enshrined in the Jingi-kan are described as radiating outward in concentric circles—from the Emperor’s body (served by the Imperial Miko), to the palace (served by the Zasama Miko), to the outer gates (served by the Mikado Miko), and finally to the land (served by the Ikushima Miko). In particular, because associated shrines such as {{ill|Zasama Shrine|de|Zasama Shrine|ja|座摩神社|zh|座摩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zasama Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 坐摩神社}} and [[:en:Ikukunitama Shrine|Ikukuni-no-tama Shrine]] remain in Naniwa, it is theorized that the rites once performed at Naniwa Palace continued into the Heian period, with the existence of the {{ill|Ya-shima Festival|de|Ya-shima Festival|ja|八十島祭|zh|八十岛祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ya-shima Festival|qq=}} during imperial enthronements emphasizing Naniwa’s importance. {{Sfn|Ancient History of Shrines|2011|p=190-192}} ; Deities of the Imperial Household Ministry (3 shrines: Son Shrine and two Kan Shrines) ::: These refer to the deities enshrined within the [[:en:Ministry of the Imperial Household|Imperial Household Ministry]], whose exact identities vary – some sources state that the Son deity protects the garden pond, others that the Kan deity wards off epidemics – but in any case they have been enshrined since before the Heian period. All are formal shrines, and their offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]; their divine Ranks were raised to Upper Third Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859). For further details, see the article on {{ill|Sonkan Shrine|de|Sonkan Shrine|ja|園韓神社|zh|园韩神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonkan Shrine|qq=}}. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Court Meals (3 shrines: Mishokutsunushi Shrine, Hurai Shrine, and Koubai Shrine) ::: These deities, under the auspices of the ministry responsible for court meals (the {{ill|Daizen-shoku|de|Daizen-shoku|ja|大膳職|zh|大膳职|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Daizen-shoku|qq=}}), include {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}, who governs food; {{ill|Hurai Shrine|de|Hurai Shrine|ja|火雷神社|zh|火雷神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hurai Shrine|qq=}}, who governs water; and {{ill|Koubai Shrine|de|Koubai Shrine|ja|高倍神社|zh|高倍神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koubai Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, associated with earthenware. In the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859), the divine Rank of {{ill|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|de|Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|ja|御食津神|zh|御食津神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mishokutsunushi-no-kami|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}} was raised to Lower Third Rank, that of Hurai Shrine to Upper Fifth Rank, and that of Koubai Shrine to Lower Fifth Rank. According to the anecdotal record [[:en:Takahashi Ujibumi|Takahashi Shibun]], see also [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/170101.html Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection – Awa Zashinja (Awa Province, Awa District)] and [{{NDLDC|1879469/56}} 'Gunsho Ruijū Fifth Volume'] in the National Diet Library Digital Collection, additional details are provided. ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Sake Production (4 shrines at O-miyaburushi Shrine; 2 shrines at Sakaden Shrine) ::: These deities, affiliated with the ministry responsible for sake brewing (the {{ill|Zōshūsai|de|Zōshūsai|ja|造酒司|zh|造酒司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zōshūsai|qq=}}), consist of the O-miyaburushi deity associated with food and sake and two deities governing the water used in brewing. All four O-miyaburushi shrines were formal shrines, with their offerings entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]]; in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859) the divine Rank of Sakaden Shrine appears to have been raised to Lower Fifth Rank, and in the 3rd year of Jōgan ([[:en:862|862年]]) the deities Sakayamitodono Otoko-no-kami and Sakayamitodono Megami were elevated to Upper Fifth Rank. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=32}} ; Deities Enshrined under the Imperial Household Ministry for Water (1 shrine) ::: This is the deity enshrined in the office of the {{ill|Shusui-shi|de|Shusui-shi|ja|主水司|zh|主水司|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shusui-shi|qq=}}, which oversees water and ice procurement—the deity being enshrined at {{ill|Narutai Shrine|de|Narutai Shrine|ja|鳴雷神社|zh|鳴雷神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Narutai Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. {{Sfn|Shikinaisha Survey Report|1979|p=33}} ; Capital Deities (3 shrines: Taishikoto-no-mikoto, Hisashimitachinomiya, and Hayai Shrine) : These are the deities enshrined within the capital of Heian-kyo, as listed in the Kami Name Register. All three are formal shrines whose offerings were entrusted during the {{ill|Monthly Festival|de|Monatsfest|ja|月次祭|zh|月次祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Monthly Festival|qq=}} and the [[:en:Niiname-no-Matsuri|Niinamesai]], and particularly the deities Taishikoto-no-mikoto and Hisashimitachinomiya were also honored at the {{ill|Sounamatsuri|de|Sounamatsuri|ja|相嘗祭|zh|相嘗祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sounamatsuri|qq=}}. ; [[:en:Ame-no-Koyane|Taitatari-no-mikoto]] :: In the Muromachi period, this deity of ritual recitations (prayers) was enshrined to the west. His divine Rank was raised to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859), later to Upper Third Rank. He is now defunct. In the Kami Name Register he appears as the formal shrine in Yamato Province—namely, the “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with Mori Shrine in [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]/[[:en:Tenri, Nara|Tenri City]]) and in Tsushima Province as “Taishikoto Shrine” (currently identified with {{ill|Taishikoto Shrine|de|Taishikoto Shrine|ja|太祝詞神社|zh|太祝詞神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taishikoto Shrine|qq=}} in [[:en:Nagasaki Prefecture|Nagasaki Prefecture]]/[[:en:Tsushima, Nagasaki|Tsushima City]]); these are regarded as his original enclosures. ; {{ill|Kushimachinomiya|de|Kushimachinomiya|ja|櫛真智命|zh|櫛真智命|lt=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_ja=久慈真智命神|lt_de=Hisashimitachinomiya|lt_zh=Hisashimitachinomiya|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushimachinomiya|qq=}} :: Enshrined to the west of the Shijōbōmon area, this divinized deity of divination was elevated to Lower Fifth Rank in the first year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (859) and is now defunct. According to the Kami Name Register, his original shrine is the “Tenkōzan Zari Kushinomiya Shrine” in Yamato Province (with candidate shrines in [[Kashihara City]] of Nara Prefecture, including Tenkōzan Shrine and Kuninotokotachi Shrine) and is considered his original. ; {{ill|Hayai Shrine|de|Hayai Shrine|ja|隼神社|zh|隼神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hayai Shrine|qq=}} :: Enshrined within the Shujakuin of the Later Palace, this deity was raised to Upper Fourth Rank in the sixteenth year of the {{ill|Jōgan Era|de|Jōgan-Ära|ja|Jōgan|zh|Jōgan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan Era|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} ([[:en:874|874年]]) and is now maintained as an associated shrine of {{ill|Mangai Shrine|de|Mangai Shrine|ja|梛神社|zh|梛神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mangai Shrine|qq=}} (located in [[:en:Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto|Nakagyo Ward]] of Kyoto City). For details, see the section "[[Mangai Shrine#Hayai Shrine]]". == == 式外社 == 『延喜式』神名帳の編纂当時に存在したが、同帳に記載の無い神社。 {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; font-size:85%" !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=2 | 文献 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" colspan=3 | 比定社 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" rowspan=2 | 集成 |- !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 神名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 記事 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 社名 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 所在地 !align="center" style="background:#a0f0a0" | 備考 |- |colspan="9" style="background-color:#C0C0C0; height:2em;"|'''[[大内裏|宮中]]''' |- |'''庭火神'''

This is a '''List of Shikinaisha in the Imperial Palace'''. Or the list of shrines in [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which is present in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. On this page we will also cover the {{ill|Shikigeisha|ja|式外社|1=Shikigeisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigeisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikigeisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延喜式神名帳|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} of [[Heian-kyō|the Imperial Palace]] which are shrines that are known to have existed at that time due to other historical records, such as the [[Rikkokushi]], but for some reason were excluded from the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}.
